So here we say: because it is defective, its original form is "la-ati" with a ya', the ya' was dropped and tanwin was put in its place: ﴿la-ata-n﴾. On this basis we say: "ata" is the predicate of "inna," raised by it, and the sign of its nominative case is a presumed damma on its end, on the omitted ya' because of the meeting of two unvocalized letters.

﴿And He﴾, that is Allah, the Exalted, ﴿is the All-Hearing﴾ of the speech of the servants, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their deeds. ﴿The All-Hearing﴾ means: possessor of hearing, nothing of what is heard is hidden from Him, every audible thing is perceived by Allah, the Exalted. Hearing, as has passed with us, is of two types: hearing of perception (sam' idrak) and hearing of response (sam' ijabah). The first is like His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the speech of the woman who pleads with you﴾ [al-Mujadilah 1]. The second is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim 39], and like the worshipper's saying: "Allah hears the one who praises Him," meaning that He answers.

We mentioned earlier that hearing of perception is divided into types: some of which imply a warning (tahdid), some which imply support and aid (nasr wa ta'yid), and some which intend mere perception. An example of the first, which is for warning?

Student: His saying: ﴿Indeed I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha 46].

Shaykh: No, we want something clear, that does not need [explanation] for this and for that.

Student: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the speech of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich"﴾ [Al 'Imran 181].

Shaykh: Yes, this one is meant as a warning. An example of what is meant as support and aid?

Student: ﴿Indeed I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha 46].

Shaykh: ﴿Indeed I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾, yes.

And an example of what is meant as mere perception, which intends merely to show that Allah encompasses the thing and hears it?

Student: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the speech of the woman who pleads with you﴾ [al-Mujadilah 1].

Shaykh: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the speech of the woman who pleads with you.﴾

And is His being All-Hearing necessarily an affirmation of an ear? The answer: it does not necessarily follow, just as His being All-Seeing does not necessarily imply affirming an eye. But the eye is affirmed by another proof. Had Allah not affirmed it for Himself by another proof, we would not affirm it. So, as for the All-Hearing, we do not say that being All-Hearing necessarily means He has an ear, just as being Speaking does not necessarily mean He has a tongue and two lips, and similar things. We know that the earth reports its news, and it reports only after hearing. Does it have an ear? As far as we know, it has no ear. Does it have a tongue? We do not know that it has a tongue. So on this basis we say: affirming hearing does not necessarily mean affirming an ear.

If someone says: it is established in the sound hadith: "Allah has never listened to anything as He listens to a prophet with a beautiful voice who chants the Quran"?

The answer: the meaning of "He listened to him" (adhina lahu) is: He listened to him. This also does not necessarily entail affirming an ear, because it is not explicit, and attributes cannot be affirmed on the basis of possibility. The matter must be clear and explicit.

Student: (...) "adhina" (...)?

Shaykh: No. "Adhina" means "qaddara" (decreed)? No, its meaning is "istama'a" (listened), because it is linked to a voice: "to a prophet with a beautiful voice who chants the Quran." Allah has given permission to people in the sense of legal permission, for example He allowed them or permitted them what is greater than this, for indeed monotheism and other things greater than the recitation of the Quran are surely permitted by Him far more.

His words: ﴿the All-Knowing﴾. The author says: (of their deeds). In reality, knowledge pertains to actions and speech also. So restricting it to actions is open to question, because what is specific to actions is only seeing, whereas knowledge is more general: it pertains to actions, pertains to speech, pertains to the inner thoughts of the soul, and pertains to what is spoken aloud, to everything.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Whoever strives﴾. The author said: (striving of war or of the self).

I forgot to say: where is the response to ﴿whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾? The author estimated it with his words "so let him prepare for it" and considered it omitted. My view is that there is no harm in saying that the response of the condition is His saying: ﴿the term of Allah is surely coming﴾, and the meaning is that whoever hopes to meet Allah, it will come to him. There is no need to estimate something omitted, because the original principle is no omission. What the author estimated is like what he estimated in His saying: ﴿Say: whoever is an enemy of Gabriel, then indeed he has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Baqarah 97]. It has already passed that the author estimated there: "so let him die of rage," and we mentioned there that there is no need for this estimate.

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: He hopes, but hope is built on love. You do not hope for a thing unless you love it, so the hope for a thing, meaning expectation of its occurrence.

He said: (﴿Whoever strives﴾ [al-'Ankabut 6]: striving of war or of the self). The author's phrase informs us that striving (jihad) is of two types: striving of war, which is by fighting enemies, and striving of the self, by striving against yourself to perform acts of obedience and to abandon forbidden things.

﴿Whoever strives, he strives only for himself﴾. He said regarding its meaning: (the benefit of his striving is for himself, not for Allah). So the one who strives, and striving is the exertion of effort in a thing, does not strive for Allah but works for himself, as in His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾ [Fussilat 46].

As for the author's saying: (the benefit of his striving is for himself, not for Allah), yes, it is for him, because he is rewarded, whether he strives against himself or against others. Although when he strives against others, the benefit may also be for the other, since through striving that other person may enter the religion of Allah, and then he gains benefit.

The point is that Allah, the Exalted, does not benefit from this striving. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds﴾. This is like a reason given for His saying: ﴿he strives only for himself﴾. Allah is free from need of it: He does not benefit from obedience nor is harmed by disobedience.

His saying: (free from need of them). What is the meaning of "ghani" (free of need)? Its meaning is the one who does not need them, because of what He possesses of generosity, abundance and management of affairs. He does not need all the worlds. The author said: (﴿the worlds﴾: mankind, jinn and angels). What comes next?

Student: (and from their worship).

Shaykh: (and from their worship), yes. He is free from need of them, He does not need them: ﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat 56–57].

Likewise, He is free from need of their worship, because their worship is only for their own sake. As for Allah, the Exalted, He does not benefit from the obedience of the obedient, nor is He harmed by the disobedience of the disobedient.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is free﴾: the sentence here is emphasized with how many emphases? With two: "inna" and the lam. ﴿Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.﴾

(﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their evil deeds﴾ [al-'Ankabut 7], by doing righteous deeds, ﴿and We will surely reward them with the best﴾, meaning "good," and its accusative is by removal of the preposition "bi" (with); ﴿of what they used to do﴾, which is the righteous deeds.)

His saying: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. This stands in contrast to ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us?﴾. Here He says: ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. Faith, as is often established, is affirmation together with acceptance and submission, not merely affirmation.

His saying: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ refers to the deeds of the limbs. Faith is in the heart, and doing righteous deeds is in the limbs. Action includes both speech and deed. For this reason it is not a counterpart to speech, as some people think when they say "speech and action." Rather, the counterpart of speech is deed, while action includes both speech and deed. So ﴿did righteous deeds﴾ includes deeds, such as bowing, prostration, prayer, standing and sitting in it, and includes speech, such as reciting the Quran, takbir and tahmid, and other things.

His saying: ﴿righteous﴾ means righteous deeds. It is an adjective of an omitted noun, its estimate being "righteous deeds." The righteous deed is the one that combines how many conditions?

Student: Sincerity and following (the Sunnah).

Shaykh: Yes, the righteous deed is the one that combines two conditions: sincerity (ikhlas) and following (mutabaʿah). Sincerity means that you intend by your deed the face of Allah, the Exalted, and the Hereafter. Following means that in this you follow the Prophet (ﷺ). The opposite of the first is associating partners (shirk), and the opposite of the second is innovation (bid'ah), so you are neither a polytheist nor an innovator.

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely remove from them their evil deeds﴾: here He said ﴿We will surely remove﴾, and the clause is the answer to an implied oath, its estimate being: "By Allah, We will surely remove." So it is emphasized with three emphases: the oath, the lam and the nun.

His saying: ﴿We will surely remove from them their evil deeds﴾. Takfir here means concealment (satr), from which comes "kuffara," the sheath that conceals the spathe of the date palm. So the meaning of "We will remove from them their evil deeds" is: We will conceal them. The concealment is meant with its consequence, which is pardon. But by what do We remove their evil deeds? By their faith and their righteous deeds, because faith erases what came before it, and about righteous deeds Allah says: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your evil deeds﴾ [al-Nisa' 31].

Student: (...)?

Shaykh: Yes, this is its concealment, because it is derived from "kufr," which is concealment.

Student: (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 29, verse 4–8 (part 2 of 4):

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is correct. Among its examples is: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your minor misdeeds﴾; because it (takfir) is derived from covering, and covering the misdeeds means removing them and not holding one accountable for them.
And His saying: ﴿We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾. The author said: (through doing righteous deeds). So their righteous deeds serve to expiate their misdeeds. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them, so long as major sins are avoided."[[Narrated by Muslim (233/16) from Abu Hurayrah.]] And he (ﷺ) said: "The 'umrah to 'umrah is an expiation for what lies between them."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1773) and Muslim (1349/437) from Abu Hurayrah.]] Thus, righteous deeds act as a covering over evil deeds, so that no trace of them remains.
He says: ﴿We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best﴾. "We will reward them": reward (jaza') means recompense for something. Regarding His saying ﴿We will surely reward them﴾, what was said concerning ﴿We will surely remove﴾ applies to the emphasis here as well.
And His saying: ﴿the best﴾. The author said: (meaning good). It seems he wished to avoid a difficulty that may be raised, namely: the verse indicates that they will be rewarded with the best of what they used to do, and "good" (hasan) and "better" (ahsan) apply to righteous deeds. So if the verse means "the best of what they used to do," does that mean that the good deeds are rewarded or not? They are not rewarded [merely as good]. Therefore the author interpreted "ahsan" as "hasan" (good): "the good of what they used to do." But we see that there is no need for this interpretation, and that what the verse indicates is preferable to what the author proposed. Allah says: "We will reward them with the best reward of what they used to do," so it is on the basis of an omitted element: "We will reward them with the best reward."
The best reward has been explained by Allah the Exalted in His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof﴾ [al-An'am 160], and the Exalted said: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah 261]. Is this reward the best reward or not? It is the best reward, because the reward's ultimate limit is to be like what the doer did; but here they are rewarded with what is better and greater. On this basis, (ahsan) is not in the accusative by the removal of the preposition, as the author said: (and its accusative is by removal of the preposition, the baa'). Rather, it is a second object of the verb (najzi), and the first object is the pronoun hu, and the nun in ﴿lanajziyannahum﴾ is for emphasis.
This is the meaning of the noble verse; that is, Allah promised them two things: the removal of misdeeds through righteous deeds, and recompense for these deeds, which is that they are given the best reward; and that a good deed will be multiplied tenfold, up to seven hundred fold, and to many more multiples.
And His saying: ﴿the best of what they used to do﴾. Why does the author say: (namely, the righteous deeds)? These righteous deeds that they do, Allah will reward them for with the best reward they are given.
Then the Exalted said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-'Ankabut 8]. When the Glorified and Exalted mentioned the general outline of His right and what He threatened against the opponents and what He promised to the compliant, He said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man (regarding) his parents﴾, that is, We have charged him concerning them; i.e., We made a covenant with him concerning them. Enjoining (wasiyyah) is only in important matters. And His saying ﴿to his parents﴾ means his mother and his father.
﴿Kindness﴾: the author said: (i.e., an enjoining that is of goodness). According to his view, ﴿husnan﴾ is a description of an omitted noun: an enjoining that is good. And "husn," as you know, is a verbal noun and not "hasan." If it is a verbal noun, then a genitive must be supposed for it, namely "possessing goodness," as the author said. It is strongly possible that ﴿husnan﴾ here is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition; that is, We made a covenant with him in goodness, and that "husn" here means "ihsan" (kindness), as the Exalted said in another verse: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-Ahqaf 15]. This is closer than the author's supposition, and Allah knows best.
A student: (...)?
The Shaykh: Yes, this is the apparent meaning itself, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿sailing under Our eyes﴾ [al-Qamar 14], meaning in Our sight, under Our eyes.
A student: The evidence from the Sunnah (...)?
The Shaykh: [It is] for one who thinks that Allah the Exalted cannot take vengeance on him for committing misdeeds; by His saying: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outrun Us?﴾
* It is also derived from it: a warning to the doers of evil deeds that Allah will seize them, and that they will not escape Allah.
* It is also derived from this: the prohibition of thinking ill of Allah; by His saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, for whoever thinks that Allah is unable to overtake him..
(...) Then the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then the term of Allah is surely coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 5].
* Among the benefits of this verse: reassurance to those who hope for the meeting with Allah that what they hope for will come.
* Second, among its benefits: the affirmation of recompense.
* Third: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection; by His saying: ﴿the term of Allah is surely coming﴾.
* And among its benefits: the affirmation of the two names ﴿All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ for Allah.
* And among its benefits: the affirmation of what the two names include of attributes; the first includes the attribute of hearing, and the second includes the attribute of knowledge.
And His saying the Exalted: ﴿And whoever strives, he strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ [al-'Ankabut 6].
* Among the benefits of this verse: that a person must necessarily encounter hardship in carrying out what is obligatory upon him; because jihad means exerting effort to attain a difficult matter.
* And among its benefits: that whoever strives in righteous deeds, his striving is for himself, and Allah does not benefit from it.
* And among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah the Glorified and Exalted's independence from His creation; by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾.
* And among its benefits: that whoever does not strive, his harm is upon himself; because if the benefit of striving is for you, then the harm of abandoning it falls upon you.
And the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-'Ankabut 7].
* Among the benefits of this verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds.
* And among its benefits: that misdeeds are expiated by it. Are the intended misdeeds the minor sins or not? The minor sins; because of His saying ﷺ: "The five prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them, so long as major sins are avoided."[[Narrated by Muslim (233/16) from Abu Hurayrah.]]
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: What is expiated by righteous deeds, [major sins] are not; there must be repentance in them.
* And among them: that the reward of Allah the Exalted is better than and superior to the deed of the believer; by His saying: ﴿and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾.
* And among its benefits: that there must be in the deed that it be righteous, and the righteous is what combines two conditions: sincerity to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and following the Messenger (ﷺ). So if it is not sincere, it is corrupt; and if it is not in accordance with the Sharia, it is also corrupt. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), the wording being his, from 'A'ishah.]]
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Affirmation (tasdiq) is part of faith.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: (...) sincerity and following.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Affirmation? Sincerity cannot be achieved except with affirmation, and following cannot be achieved except with affirmation; faith precedes...
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That faith means affirmation?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Acceptance requires faith; faith is a condition for acceptance. Any person who is not a believer, no deed of his is accepted; affirmation preceding the righteous deed is necessary, then sincerity; there is no sincerity except with affirmation. How can you be sincere to one you do not affirm? Or how can you follow one you do not affirm? So sincerity and following imply affirmation.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The well-known position among the people of knowledge is two conditions, and there is no third condition; two conditions only.
* * *
He says: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-'Ankabut 8]. Enjoining (wasiyyah) means a covenant concerning an important matter; so "wassaynahu" means: We made a covenant with him concerning an important matter so that he would carry it out.
And His saying ﴿to his parents﴾ means his mother and his father.
And His saying ﴿kindness﴾ is an object of ﴿We enjoined﴾, or it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition; that is, We made a covenant with him in goodness, i.e., in kindness to both of them. There is no need for what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (i.e., an enjoining of goodness, by being dutiful to them). Rather, what is enjoined, what is it? The very goodness itself, and goodness here is not a description of the enjoining but a description of what is enjoined. The author intends by his supposition that goodness be a description of Allah's enjoining, whereas the correct view is that it is a description of what? Of what is enjoined; that is, We enjoined him with a matter possessing kindness, as the Exalted said: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-Ahqaf 15].
And the author's saying: (by being dutiful to them): what is birr?
Birr is kindness (...). One is kind to them by speech, by action, and by wealth; and wealth in reality is from action. So one is kind to them by speech, due to the Exalted's saying: ﴿And speak to them a noble word﴾ [al-Isra' 23]; by action: ﴿And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy﴾ [al-Isra' 24]; and by wealth: ﴿And give the relative his right, and the needy﴾ [al-Isra' 26]. For example, if a person is generous to his parents with wealth but (...) toward them (...) never, having overwhelmed them with wealth, yet he is aloof from them in speech, harsh toward them, frowning in their faces, has he performed birr? No. Likewise, if he is smiling to them and gentle with them in speech, lavishing wealth upon them, but does not serve them himself when the need calls for it, he is not dutiful; birr must be by speech, action, and wealth.
He said: ﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾ [al-'Ankabut 8].
﴿If they strive with you﴾: that is, they exerted their effort. You know that jihad means compulsion, coercion, and pressure.
﴿They strive with you to make you associate with Me﴾: meaning they commanded you to associate partners and exerted effort in that by compulsion and pressure: at times by praising shirk, at times by denouncing monotheism, at times by compulsion and coercion, and at times by threatening severance. If they strive with you in this, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿do not obey them﴾. Why? Because the right of the Creator takes precedence over the right of the created, and associating partners with Allah is injustice toward the Creator, as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, association with Allah is great injustice﴾ [Luqman 13]. So it is not permissible to neglect the right of Allah for the sake of the right of these people.
His saying ﴿they strive with you to make you associate with Me﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me﴾ [Luqman 15].
His saying ﴿to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge﴾ (i.e., by their association) ﴿knowledge﴾. The author says: (agreement with reality, so it has no implicit restriction).
Notice the verse ﴿to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge﴾. Would someone say: "If they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have knowledge, then obey them"?
If we took the apparent meaning of the verse, we would say it indicates that association with Allah divides into two kinds: association for which there is knowledge, and association for which there is no knowledge; so association for which there is knowledge is permissible, and association for which there is no knowledge is not permissible.
We say: the matter is not so; rather, this is a statement of reality that every association with Allah is something for which a person has no knowledge. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿and that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority﴾ [al-A'raf 33]. And it is known that Allah the Exalted did not make any association for which there is authority; all association has no authority. Rather, the authority and sound knowledge have established that it is false, or not? That it is false. So the meaning of His saying ﴿of which you have no knowledge﴾ becomes that it agrees with reality, and so it serves as a rationale for prohibiting shirk; as if He says: "to make you associate with Me while the reality is that you have no knowledge of shirk." For shirk definitely cannot be established by evidence; rather, the sound evidence is for its non-existence, since Allah the Exalted has no partner.
(﴿So do not obey them﴾ in associating partners.) If the father and mother say, for example: "If you do not associate, we will cut you off, we will not speak to you, and we will not come to your house." What do you say about this?
* The students: They are not obeyed.
* The Shaykh: They are not obeyed whatever the matter; because this is the meaning of His saying ﴿And if they strive﴾.
﴿So do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾: its meaning is: do not think that by disobeying them you will incur sin in this; for your return is to Me, when? On the Day of Resurrection.
﴿and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾: the intended "informing" here implies its consequence, which is punishment and accountability; so you remained upon monotheism and will be recompensed as a monotheist, and they remained upon shirk and will be recompensed as polytheists; indeed, even more than that, they will be recompensed as polytheists who call to shirk. That is, they did not strive with you to associate partners except that they persisted in it and insisted upon it, so there will be two punishments upon them: one punishment for their association, and the second punishment for their calling you to shirk; indeed, not merely calling, but striving with the child to make him associate partners.
﴿To Me is your return﴾: meaning you and they.
﴿and I will inform you of what you used to do﴾: I will tell you; and the intended "telling" implies its consequence, which is why the author said: (and I will recompense you for it).
* * *
﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾ [al-'Ankabut 9]. Allah has explained earlier that those who believe and do righteous deeds, Allah will remove their misdeeds from them and reward them with the best of what they used to do. Here is another reward, which is that He will admit them among the righteous. The lam in ﴿We will surely admit them﴾ introduces an oath, and the nun is for emphasis, so the sentence is emphasized with three emphatics.
And His saying ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾: are they not righteous?
The answer: Yes, they are righteous ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, but the intended "the righteous" are those who preceded them and guided them to good, and they are the prophets; and the prophets are without doubt among the righteous. The prophets, peace be upon them, would meet the Prophet (ﷺ) during the Mi'raj and say: "Welcome, the righteous brother and the righteous prophet."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3887) and Muslim (164/264) from Malik ibn Sasa'ah.]] So they described him with righteousness. Likewise, in Surat al-Anbiya' He said: ﴿Each of them was of the patient, and We admitted them into Our mercy; indeed, they were of the righteous﴾ [al-Anbiya' 85–86]. There is no doubt that the people most specifically described with righteousness are the prophets, because they are righteous and reformers, peace be upon them.

The author said, may Allah have mercy on him: "(﴿Among the righteous﴾: the prophets and the saints, by Our causing them to be gathered with them)." His words "and the saints" are open to question, because those who believed and did righteous deeds are the saints (awliya'). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:257]. He, glorified and exalted, also says: ﴿Indeed, the friends of Allah—there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Yunus 10:62]. He, exalted, says: ﴿Your only guardian is Allah, and His Messenger, and those who believe—those who establish prayer and give zakah, while bowing [in worship]﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:55], and so on to the end. But (the author's intent) is that they are to be admitted among the prophets, because the rank of the prophets is higher than the rank of the saints.

* A student: O Shaykh, the verse: Allah says, ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger—those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets...﴾

* The Shaykh: ﴿...and the truthful, and the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:69].

* The student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: (...) because these are the more fitting. And Allah did not mention in this verse four categories; He mentioned only one category... (...) the righteous; the prophets, and the categories—correct—are four: those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour: the prophets, which includes the messengers; the truthful; the martyrs; and the righteous. The righteous are a general category covering all believers. But know that every righteous person is a friend (wali) of Allah.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, because wilayah (being a friend of Allah) is more general. Even the prophets are among the awliya' in the general sense.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The situation is that the author says they will be gathered with them. That means that on the Day of Resurrection they will be gathered with the prophets. It does not mean that they will attain their rank. The prophets are higher than them, as Allah says: ﴿Then those will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour of the prophets and the truthful﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:69]. The Prophet (ﷺ) has the banner, and everyone who believed in him will be gathered in his company.

* * *

﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah"﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:10]. The ﴿min﴾ here is partitive (lil-tab'id), and it is the predicate placed first, while ﴿man﴾ is the postponed subject: ﴿man yaqulu﴾ ("those who say").

His words ﴿those who say "We believe"﴾ mean that they say it with their tongues, but faith has not taken root in their hearts. Therefore ﴿when they are harmed for the sake of Allah, they consider the persecution of people to be like the punishment of Allah﴾. So he says with his tongue, "We believe in Allah," ﴿but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾, meaning he suffers harm, ﴿for Allah﴾, meaning for the religion of Allah, the religion he adheres to. It is also possible that ﴿fi﴾ is causal (lil-sababiyyah), meaning "because of Allah," that is, because of his standing up for the religion of Allah. The meaning is one whether we take it as locative or causal.

﴿When he is harmed for Allah﴾ is a conditional clause. Its response is: ﴿he considers the persecution of people to be like the punishment of Allah﴾, meaning their harm to him, ﴿like the punishment of Allah﴾ in terms of fear of it, so he obeys them and becomes a hypocrite. He considers the persecution of people, meaning their harming him, because harming a believer by others is a trial by which a person is tested. Some people—we ask Allah for well-being—when they are harmed for Allah, they do not endure. Some people who are firm in their faith, if they are harmed, endure and their faith grows stronger. But this one who said "We believe in Allah" does not have firm faith in his heart. ﴿When he is harmed for Allah, he considers the persecution of people to be like the punishment of Allah﴾ in terms of fear of it. So he regards this as a punishment. What then happens? He apostatizes because of this harm and says, "This is a punishment, so I will return from what I am upon," and then he becomes a hypocrite. Yet despite this he claims to be a believer. When does he claim to be a believer?

﴿And if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you"﴾. Note that ﴿wa-la'in jaa'a﴾ ("and if there comes"). The author says that it is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam) and "in" (if). What is "in"? It is a conditional particle, and ﴿jaa'a﴾ is the verb of the condition, and the clause ﴿la-yaqulunna﴾ is the response?

* A student: The response of the condition.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not its response; it is the response of the oath. That is why it is introduced by the lam, ﴿la-yaqulunna﴾. When an oath and a condition come together, Ibn Malik says:

*Omit, when a condition and an oath come together, the response of whichever is placed later; it is then obligatory to omit it.*

Here, which one is placed later, the condition or the oath? The condition. So its response is omitted, because the response of the oath indicates it.

(﴿And if victory comes﴾ to the believers ﴿from your Lord﴾, and they gain spoils), ﴿la-yaqulunna﴾: is this plural or singular?

* The students: Plural.

* The Shaykh: ﴿la-yaqulunna﴾ is plural. So the pronoun returned to ﴿man﴾ in the words of Allah, ﴿those who say, "We believe in Allah"﴾, according to meaning. And it returned to it at the start—﴿man yaqulu﴾, and He did not say "man yaquluna"—according to the wording. This rule has come up for us more than once, and we said: when a relative pronoun or a general conditional noun, applying to one or many, is used, it is permissible for its pronoun to be plural or singular. If the wording is observed, it is singular; if the meaning is observed, it agrees with what is intended by meaning. This applies whether the noun is a conditional noun or a relative noun. What we have now is the relative noun.

In conditional nouns, Allah says in Surat al-Talaq: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteousness—He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah has certainly given for him a good provision﴾ [al-Talaq 65:11]. Here the wording is observed (﴿yud'khilhu﴾, singular), then the meaning is observed (﴿khalidina fiha﴾, plural), then the wording is observed again (﴿qad ahsana Allahu lahu rizqan﴾, singular). So this verse contains observing the wording, then observing the meaning, then observing the wording a second time.

He said: (﴿la-yaqulunna﴾: the nun of the nominative has been dropped because of the accumulation of nuns, and the waw is the plural pronoun, and it is dropped because two consonants came together, and the damma remains—﴿la-yaqulunna﴾—indicating the dropped waw). (﴿Indeed, we were with you﴾ in faith, so give us a share of the spoils.) I seek refuge in Allah! These people, when they are harmed for Allah, turn back on their heels and side with those who harmed them, but when victory comes to the believers, they say, "We were with you," meaning, "we want to receive what you received of the spoils." Allah says in response to them: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾ What is the answer? "Yes."

As for His words ﴿Is not Allah most knowing?﴾ the author said: (That is, "is not Allah a knower?"). We have already noted that this kind of statement is not considered an explanation but a distortion, because "a'lam" (most knowing) is more emphatic than "'alim" (knowing). How could he reduce it to "'alim", which is weaker!

As for His words ﴿of what is in the breasts of the worlds﴾, what is meant by "what is in their breasts" is their hearts, meaning: He is more knowing of people's hearts, because the heart is located in the chest, and the heart is the seat of intention. In this, Allah willing, there is evidence that the seat of affirmation and denial is the heart.

As for His words (of what is in their hearts of faith and hypocrisy), the answer is: "Yes."

Accordingly, we say to this person who said, "I am with you," we say: you are not truly with them, because you have become a disbeliever in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, when you apostatized after being harmed.

* * *

﴿And Allah will surely make known those who believed, and He will surely make known the hypocrites﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:11]. ﴿la-ya'lamanna Allah﴾: is it in the future or the past? In the future, because when the emphatic nun (nun al-tawkid) enters a present-tense verb, it makes it refer to the future. This sentence is emphasized with three emphatics: the oath, the lam, and the emphatic nun. The knowledge meant here, which Allah emphasized and made future, what is meant by knowledge in ﴿wa-la-ya'lamanna Allah﴾?

* A student: Knowledge of witnessing.

* The Shaykh: Yes, knowledge of witnessing and of recompense. Because Allah, exalted, knows the hypocrite and the believer before this. But His prior knowledge is knowledge that this will happen, and His subsequent knowledge is knowledge that it has occurred. Second, His prior knowledge does not entail recompense, since there is no recompense except after testing, whereas His subsequent knowledge entails recompense. So whenever we see that Allah, exalted, expresses His knowledge in the Qur'an in the future tense, we interpret it as what? As knowledge of witnessing and recompense, not as the prior knowledge from eternity, because the prior knowledge from eternity is established before people were created, let alone before they act. But the knowledge that entails recompense and witnessing is what occurs afterward and takes place.

(﴿And Allah will surely make known those who believed﴾ with their hearts). The author said "with their hearts," meaning not with their tongues. The one mentioned earlier, ﴿those who say "We believe in Allah"﴾, is faith with the tongue, but this faith with the tongue does not benefit them with Allah. It is true that it benefits them in this world, which is why the Prophet (ﷺ) did not kill the hypocrites even though he knew them. He refrained from that because their outward appearance was Islam. If he had killed them, that would have been a means for a Muslim to be killed on the pretext that he was a hypocrite, while his heart is known only to Allah. The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4905) and Muslim (2584/63), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah]. Praise be to Allah, this is what the Shari'ah requires, because if the matter were otherwise, every oppressive ruler in our time would see a religious person and say he is a hypocrite and a hidden disbeliever, and then kill him. But by the grace of Allah, the Shari'ah made judgment in this world based on outward appearances, while in the Hereafter it is based on hidden realities.

﴿And Allah will surely make known those who believed, and He will surely make known the hypocrites﴾ (and He will recompense both groups). The believer is recompensed as a believer, and the hypocrite is recompensed as a hypocrite. The recompense of the hypocrite is that he is in the lowest level of the Fire, and we seek refuge in Allah: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will not find for them any helper﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:145].

He said: (The lam in the two verbs is the lam of oath). Where are the two verbs? ﴿wa-la-ya'lamanna Allah alladhina amanu﴾ and ﴿la-ya'lamanna﴾, and the second, ﴿wa-la-ya'lamanna al-munafiqin﴾. The second is the lam of oath. So the sentence is emphasized with three emphatics.

* A student: What is the meaning of His words ﴿they consider the persecution of people to be like the punishment of Allah﴾ (...)?

* The Shaykh: This may mean that they consider it like the punishment of Allah, which Allah knows. That is, they treat it as if it were a punishment, even though they themselves do not believe this.

* * *

(...) * First: the obligation to be good to one's parents in speech, action, and wealth.

* Second: affirming the mercy of Allah, the Exalted, in that He enjoined upon man (to honour) his parents.

* Third: that parents have a right even if they are disbelievers. From where do we derive this?

* A student: ﴿wa-in jahadaka﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:8]. They are polytheists who also strive (to make you associate partners), yet Allah obligated goodness toward them.

* Among its benefits: there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator, based on His words ﴿do not obey them﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the obligation to obey them in what is not sinful, because He only forbade obeying them in sin.

Here, pay attention, everyone, because this may need discussion. It is said that a person is forbidden to obey his parents in shirk and silence is kept about obeying them in what is not shirk. Let us make the prohibition more general: He forbade obeying them in sin and kept silent about obeying them in what is not sin, or not? What is forbidden is (...). Everyone, what is forbidden is obeying them in sin. Obeying them in what is not sin is left unaddressed. Let us see:

Obeying them in what is obligatory is obligatory, because Allah obligated it, such as if your father tells you, "Go and pray with the congregation," then it is obligatory upon you to pray.

Obeying them in what is neither obedience nor sin, does the verse indicate obligation or not?

It does not indicate obligation. But if obeying them includes goodness toward them, then the verse indicates obligation, based on His words ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:8]. If obeying them does not include goodness toward them, then the verse does not indicate obligation. This is why Shaykh al-Islam said: obeying parents is obligatory only in what benefits them and does not harm him. The verse supports what the Shaykh said, because Allah forbade obeying them in sin and kept silent about obeying them in what is not sin.

Let us see: obeying them in what is not sin, if it includes goodness toward them, is obligatory, based on His words ﴿and to parents, goodness﴾. So if your father, for example, asks you to go and buy something from the market, it is obligatory upon you, because it is goodness toward him, so you must do it.

If your father tells you not to keep company with so-and-so because he is upright, is it obligatory on you or not?

* The students: It is not obligatory.

* The Shaykh: It is not obligatory, because that causes harm, or at least (...), but it brings no benefit to him.

If he says, "Do not keep company with so-and-so," because there is a personal enmity between him and that person, and you have no benefit from his company nor harm from avoiding it, is obeying him obligatory? Yes, obeying him is obligatory, because keeping company with your father's enemy angers your father, so there is benefit in it.

So the main point now is: the rule in this matter is, if they command you to do something sinful, do you obey them or not?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: Good. If your father tells you, "Do not perform Hajj this year," and you are able to perform Hajj with your money and body and have not yet performed the obligatory Hajj, do you obey him or not?

* The students: No.

* The Shaykh: You do not obey him. It is obligatory upon you to perform Hajj, even if he is not pleased.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: If he is in need, then it is considered: if there is no one else who can take your place and he is dependent on you, then return, because Hajj falls away from you in that case.

If he tells you not to perform Hajj this year, and it is a voluntary Hajj, and he has no real interest in it, but only says, "My son, there are many pilgrims (...)," then obedience is not obligatory, but it is permissible, because it is not an obligation. If we say it is permissible but not obligatory, then a person should consider what follows from his travel. Perhaps the father cannot be at ease while his son has gone to that great crowd and remains anxious throughout his son's absence. In that case, what is preferable? Obedience and not traveling. But if we know he does not care, or that he is merely offering advice and is not affected, then obeying him in this matter is not obligatory, although it is still proper to be considerate toward him as far as possible.

* A student: If he says, "Divorce your wife."

* The Shaykh: If he says, "Divorce your wife," you are not obliged to comply unless there is a legitimate benefit in it, such as the father having learned something that makes it unacceptable for your wife to remain with you.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: If there is personal enmity between him and her, it is not obligatory on you. But in such a case you can accommodate him by moving her to another place, so that she is away from him, he is at ease, and she is at ease.

Now, as for the action of Ibn 'Umar toward his father, this was raised against Imam Ahmad when a man asked him about a man whose father orders him to divorce his wife. He said: "Do not divorce her." The man said: "Did not 'Umar order Ibn 'Umar to divorce his wife, and then the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to divorce her?!" He said: "Yes, that happened, but is your father 'Umar?"

What did he say? Neither "no" nor "yes"? Of course: no, he is not 'Umar.

So the noble verse indicates the prohibition of obeying them in disobedience to Allah, and it is silent about obeying them in what is not disobedience. Accordingly, obeying them is not obligatory except when it falls under the beginning of the verse, what is it? When it is kindness toward them. When there is kindness to them in it, it is obligatory by His saying: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, he is not obliged to answer (...).
* What is derived from this verse: the obligation of obeying them in matters other than the disobedience of Allah, if that is part of kindness to them.
* From the benefits of the verse: that the right of Allah is greater than all rights. Does the right of His Prophet enter into this? Yes, it enters into it; the right of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, upon you is greater than the right of your parents.
* From the benefits of the verse: that associating partners with Allah is something for which no evidence can stand; rather, all the evidences are against it and show its falsehood.
* From it: the affirmation of resurrection and return to Allah; by His saying: ﴿To Me is your return﴾.
* From the benefits of the verse also: that a person will be recompensed for his deeds; by His saying: ﴿Then I will inform you of what you used to do﴾.
* From it: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge. From where do we take it? ﴿Then I will inform you﴾; because "inform" (inbaʾ) means to tell, and telling is only about knowledge.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾.

* From the benefits of the verse: the virtue of faith and righteous deeds.
* From its benefits: that by them one reaches joining the righteous; by His saying: ﴿We will surely admit them among the righteous﴾.
* From its benefits: that faith alone is not sufficient for joining the righteous.
* From it: that deeds are not beneficial unless they are righteous, which is what combines the two conditions: sincerity to Allah and following the Messenger ﷺ.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah, he regards the trial from people as like the punishment of Allah﴾.

* From its benefits: that faith by the tongue alone does not benefit.
* From it: the wisdom of Allah, exalted is He, in testing a person with the harm people inflict upon him for his faith.
* From the benefits of the verse: that trial is the touchstone by which the truthful is distinguished from others; otherwise every person would say, "I am a believer."
* From it: that whoever faith has not taken firm root in his heart turns away from it when he is harmed for it.
* From it: that the hypocrites claim to share with the believers in times of ease and part from them in hardships.

* Student: In times of ease (...).

* The Shaykh: In times of ease, generally (...) all the more so; and they part from them in times of hardship: when they are harmed for Allah, they apostatize.

* From the benefits of the verse also: that victory is from Allah.
* From it: a warning against hypocrisy; by His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾

* From the benefits of the verse in His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely make known﴾: that the wisdom of the test is to make clear the believer from the hypocrite.
* From it: the affirmation of hypocrisy; by His saying: ﴿And Allah will surely make known the hypocrites﴾.
* From it: that the hypocrites are not believers. From where do we take it?
He made the hypocrites a counterpart to the believers, and the counterpart of a thing is its opposite.
* From it: the affirmation of Allah, glorified and exalted, knowing what is in the hearts.
* From it: that faith's seat is the heart and not the limbs; for if it were the limbs, the hypocrites would be believers. Faith's seat is the heart.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 29, verses 12–13 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way,"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 12] "our religion"). It means: our path. As-sabil (the way) means at-tariq (the path). This is from the propaganda and the calling to falsehood. The disbelievers say to the believers who have believed in the Messenger ﷺ: ﴿"Follow our way"﴾, that is, our path, which is shirk.

﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾. The lam here is the lam of command, but what is meant is a statement of information; that is: "And we will bear your sins." They expressed the statement in the form of a command to show their commitment to this for them, the commitment of whom? Of the disbelievers to the believers in this. That is, instead of saying "And we will bear," it is as if they are saying, "We bind ourselves to this, we bind ourselves and direct the matter to ourselves."

﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾. Al-khatayا (the sins) is the plural of khati'ah (sin), which is committing wrongdoing. That is, your committing wrongdoing, we will bear it.

(﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾ in following us, if there are any, and the command is in the sense of information.)

His saying "if there are any" – the author (al-Mu'allif) estimated it because these polytheists who called to following them do not believe that they are in error. They say to the believers: "Follow our way, and if there are sins for you in this following, we will bear them." So the estimation mentioned by the author is clear from the verse, because if they believed that when they returned to shirk or entered into shirk they would be in error, they would not have called to shirk. Their saying ﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾ means: if there are sins for you in entering shirk, we will bear them.

This statement contains a call and propaganda. The call is ﴿"Follow our way"﴾, and the propaganda is the adorning of this matter for them; their saying ﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾, meaning: there is nothing upon you.

Allah the Exalted said, denying what they claimed: ﴿"And they will not bear anything of their sins."﴾

﴿"And they will not bear"﴾: (ma) is a negative particle, and here it is of the Hijazi type, and the bi' (ba) entered on its predicate in the manner of the saying of Ibn Malik:

"And after (ma) and (laysa) the ba' makes the predicate genitive..." ...........................

So here after (ma) He said: ﴿"they will not bear"﴾, and He brought the superfluous ba' for emphasis of the negation; that is, this is an emphasized matter: ﴿"they will not bear anything of their sins"﴾.

His saying ﴿"of anything"﴾: min is also a superfluous particle, and the benefit of its addition is to emphasize generality, whether this thing is little or much.

As for His saying ﴿"of their sins"﴾, it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of ﴿"anything"﴾; because the qualifier, when it precedes the indefinite noun, becomes a hal of it, and if it comes after, it becomes a na't (adjective).

He says: ﴿"They will not bear anything of their sins"﴾, that is: they will not bear any part of their sins. Is this a report about a legislated ruling or about a legislated ruling that is also a divine decree (qadari)?

As for it being about a legislated ruling, yes: it is not possible for these to bear anything of the sins of those, because of His saying: ﴿"And no bearer bears the burden of another"﴾ [Al-An'am 164]. As for it being about a decreed ruling as well, it is because if they had said to them, they would be lying; if they said, "We will bear your sins," they would be lying in that, because of His saying: ﴿"When those who were followed disown those who followed"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 166]. So if they said "they will not bear," it is as if Allah denies them; He says: ﴿"And they will not bear"﴾, that is, they are not truthful in what they said. So this verse now contains negation as a legislated ruling and negation as an actual reality. In the law they do not bear their burdens, and in reality they also do not bear their burdens. If they said it, they were not truthful; they will not bear anything of their sins, but they want to deceive them and delude them. And they will not bear anything of their sins. For this reason He said: ﴿"Indeed they are liars"﴾: they are liars in what? In their saying ﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾; they are liars in this. Since His saying ﴿"Indeed they are liars"﴾ may give the impression that they will not be made to bear any of their own burdens, that is, that the callers will not be made to bear any of the burdens of those they called, He said: ﴿"And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 13]. ﴿"And they will surely bear"﴾: the agent is who? The callers or those called? The callers. ﴿"And they will surely bear"﴾, and this sentence is emphasized by the oath, the lam, and the nun.

(﴿"their burdens"﴾: their sins.)

That is, the punishment of sins, and sins are called burdens because they weigh down – we seek refuge with Allah – their bearer. His saying ﴿"their burdens"﴾: does the pronoun in (hum) refer to the callers or to those called? To the callers. That is: these callers will surely bear the burdens of themselves; also ﴿"and burdens along with their burdens"﴾, other burdens along with their burdens. What are the other burdens? The burdens of their calling. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿"That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear"﴾ [An-Nahl 25]. So they bear their burdens in full, but they do not bear the burdens of those called in full; if they bore them in full, nothing would remain for those called. For this reason here He said: ﴿"and burdens along with their burdens"﴾, with ﴿"burdens"﴾ indefinite, and in the second verse He said: ﴿"and of the burdens of those whom they misled"﴾. That is because the caller does not bear the burden of the one called in full; if he bore it in full, nothing would remain for the one called, but it will be for this and for that, we seek refuge with Allah.

﴿"and burdens along with their burdens"﴾ for their calling to misguidance. Everyone who calls to misguidance has the like of the burden of whoever acts upon it, without the burdens of those people being reduced in any way.

(﴿"and burdens along with their burdens"﴾ by their saying to the believers: ﴿"Follow our way"﴾, and misguiding those who follow them.) And who are the followers? Those who followed them, because the disbelievers have leaders and followers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿"And We made them leaders calling to the Fire"﴾ [Al-Qasas 41]. Does the imam have a follower who is led by him? He has one who is led by him and follows him. So the disbelievers have leaders and have followers; these followers bear what the leaders bear of their burdens, and likewise the burdens of those they call without knowledge. But if they call a person and he does not follow them, they bear only the burden of the calling, not the burden of the action, and the reason is that there is no action.

﴿"And burdens along with their burdens. And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 13].

﴿"They will surely be questioned"﴾: who will question them? Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

﴿"on the Day of Resurrection"﴾: that is, in the Hereafter. It has already been mentioned that it is called that for three matters: the rising of people from their graves, the establishment of justice, and the standing of the witnesses; the witnesses stand on that day, justice is established in it, and people rise from their graves.

Because they said: ﴿"Follow our way, and let us bear your sins"﴾, and they are liars in this, are they not? They are liars. So they will be questioned about this lie, and likewise every deceiver who calls to his falsehood by lying will be questioned about this lie.

﴿"about what they used to fabricate"﴾: the author said: (a question of rebuke). Or a question of seeking information?
* The students: Rebuke.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 29, verses 12–13 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way,"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 12] "our religion"). It means: our path. As-sabil (the way) means at-tariq (the path). This is from the propaganda and the calling to falsehood. The disbelievers say to the believers who have believed in the Messenger ﷺ: ﴿"Follow our way"﴾, that is, our path, which is shirk.

﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾. The lam here is the lam of command, but what is meant is a statement of information; that is: "And we will bear your sins." They expressed the statement in the form of a command to show their commitment to this for them, the commitment of whom? Of the disbelievers to the believers in this. That is, instead of saying "And we will bear," it is as if they are saying, "We bind ourselves to this, we bind ourselves and direct the matter to ourselves."

﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾. Al-khatayا (the sins) is the plural of khati'ah (sin), which is committing wrongdoing. That is, your committing wrongdoing, we will bear it.

(﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾ in following us, if there are any, and the command is in the sense of information.)

His saying "if there are any" – the author (al-Mu'allif) estimated it because these polytheists who called to following them do not believe that they are in error. They say to the believers: "Follow our way, and if there are sins for you in this following, we will bear them." So the estimation mentioned by the author is clear from the verse, because if they believed that when they returned to shirk or entered into shirk they would be in error, they would not have called to shirk. Their saying ﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾ means: if there are sins for you in entering shirk, we will bear them.

This statement contains a call and propaganda. The call is ﴿"Follow our way"﴾, and the propaganda is the adorning of this matter for them; their saying ﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾, meaning: there is nothing upon you.

Allah the Exalted said, denying what they claimed: ﴿"And they will not bear anything of their sins."﴾

﴿"And they will not bear"﴾: (ma) is a negative particle, and here it is of the Hijazi type, and the bi' (ba) entered on its predicate in the manner of the saying of Ibn Malik:

"And after (ma) and (laysa) the ba' makes the predicate genitive..." ...........................

So here after (ma) He said: ﴿"they will not bear"﴾, and He brought the superfluous ba' for emphasis of the negation; that is, this is an emphasized matter: ﴿"they will not bear anything of their sins"﴾.

His saying ﴿"of anything"﴾: min is also a superfluous particle, and the benefit of its addition is to emphasize generality, whether this thing is little or much.

As for His saying ﴿"of their sins"﴾, it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of ﴿"anything"﴾; because the qualifier, when it precedes the indefinite noun, becomes a hal of it, and if it comes after, it becomes a na't (adjective).

He says: ﴿"They will not bear anything of their sins"﴾, that is: they will not bear any part of their sins. Is this a report about a legislated ruling or about a legislated ruling that is also a divine decree (qadari)?

As for it being about a legislated ruling, yes: it is not possible for these to bear anything of the sins of those, because of His saying: ﴿"And no bearer bears the burden of another"﴾ [Al-An'am 164]. As for it being about a decreed ruling as well, it is because if they had said to them, they would be lying; if they said, "We will bear your sins," they would be lying in that, because of His saying: ﴿"When those who were followed disown those who followed"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 166]. So if they said "they will not bear," it is as if Allah denies them; He says: ﴿"And they will not bear"﴾, that is, they are not truthful in what they said. So this verse now contains negation as a legislated ruling and negation as an actual reality. In the law they do not bear their burdens, and in reality they also do not bear their burdens. If they said it, they were not truthful; they will not bear anything of their sins, but they want to deceive them and delude them. And they will not bear anything of their sins. For this reason He said: ﴿"Indeed they are liars"﴾: they are liars in what? In their saying ﴿"And let us bear your sins"﴾; they are liars in this. Had they said something they were not truthful about, just as with respect to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, it is not possible that He would transfer the burdens of these to those; He said: ﴿"And no bearer bears the burden of another"﴾ [Al-An'am 164].

Since His saying ﴿"Indeed they are liars"﴾ may give the impression that they will not be made to bear any of their own burdens, that is, that the callers will not be made to bear any of the burdens of those they called, He said: ﴿"And they will surely bear their burdens and burdens along with their burdens"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 13]. ﴿"And they will surely bear"﴾: the agent is who? The callers or those called? The callers. ﴿"And they will surely bear"﴾, and this sentence is emphasized by the oath, the lam, and the nun.

(﴿"their burdens"﴾: their sins.)

That is, the punishment of sins, and sins are called burdens because they weigh down – we seek refuge with Allah – their bearer. There are people who say: lying is of two kinds, white and black. The black is what carries punishment, and the white carries no punishment. The truth is that all lying is black; there is no white in it. They say: black is what involves consuming the property of others, or aggression against them, or violating their honor; that is, what harms others. This is black. As for what serves to relax the self, reconciliation, and what is other than that, this is white. This is not correct; rather, a warning has come upon the one who lies to make people laugh [[Abu Dawud (4990) and al-Tirmidhi (2315) both from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, the wording being al-Tirmidhi's, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "Woe to the one who speaks a statement to make the people laugh, and lies. Woe to him, woe to him."]]. A person must avoid all lying, and the basic principle is that it is forbidden.

* A student: We have now said that the callers to misguidance (...) the called (...), there will be for the callers the like of it.
* The Shaykh: Yes, of what they were affected by from their calling. As for the other evil deeds, nothing of them is upon them.

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, they will bear their burdens, but if they did something that had nothing to do with the call (to the religion), then nothing of it would be upon those (others).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 29, verse 14:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people﴾ [al-'Ankabut 14]. The lam is a lam of oath (lam al-muwatta'ah lil-qasam), "qad" is for emphasis (lil-tahqiq), and the sentence is reinforced by three emphasizers. Allah emphasized this even though the address was not to one who denies it. But it has already been explained to us that important matters are emphasized even when they are not addressed to someone who denies or doubts them; all important matters are emphasized.

As for His saying ﴿We sent Noah﴾, meaning: We sent him with a message. This occurred after a long period from Adam, since people after Adam were on a single religion without a messenger, because Adam was a prophet (nabi) and not a messenger (rasul), as there was no one to whom he was sent. Rather, a law (shar') was revealed to him, he worshipped by it, and his children followed it. But when the children of Adam multiplied, their opinions and desires differed, so they needed a messenger. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Mankind were one community, and Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good news and warners, and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between people concerning that over which they differed﴾ [al-Baqarah 213]. Thus Allah the Glorified and Exalted made clear when the messengers were sent: after people had differed. For this there is a reading: "Mankind were one community, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets," and this reading is indicated by the end of the verse: ﴿to judge between people concerning that over which they differed﴾. So Allah sent Noah, and he was the first messenger sent to humankind.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, it has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, but we do not know whether this is authentic or not, because Ibn 'Abbas was among those who took knowledge from the Children of Israel.

﴿We sent Noah to his people﴾. He said: (And his age was forty years or more). (...) If it is more, the matter is easy. We do not know his exact age; we do not know it. But we know with certainty that Allah sent him while he was of an age suitable to be qualified for prophethood, whether he was forty years or more, and I do not think he was younger than that.

As for His saying ﴿to his people﴾, this contains evidence for the authentic hadith: "Every prophet was sent specifically to his people, but I have been sent to all mankind" [agreed upon by al-Bukhari (335) and Muslim (521/3), the wording being al-Bukhari's, from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah].

He said: (﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾ calling them to the Oneness of Allah, but they denied him).

﴿He remained among them﴾, meaning: in calling them to the religion of Allah.

﴿A thousand years less fifty years﴾. How much is that? Nine hundred and fifty years calling them to the worship of Allah. A long life, and he was with them in conflict. In Surah Nuh Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said: "O my people, I am to you a clear warner. [Worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me. He will forgive you of your sins and delay you until a specified term. Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not delayed, if you only knew.] He said: "My Lord, I have invited my people night and day, but my invitation has increased them only in flight. And indeed, every time I invited them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments and persisted and were arrogant with [great] arrogance. Then I invited them openly. Then I announced to them and declared to them secretly"﴾ [Nuh 2-9]. Look at the stages of this great call, and yet they gained nothing. Only a few believed with him. The period is long, the call is varied, and the opposition and hostility toward Noah is severe and great. They would pass by him while he was building the ship and mock him, but he remained firm in faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and said: ﴿If you mock us, then indeed we mock you as you mock. And you will know who will receive a punishment that will disgrace him and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ [Hud 38-39]. About this long period, Allah the Exalted says in Surah Hud: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud 40], and even one of his sons did not believe. This obliges us to be patient and to seek reward from Allah.

When one of us calls people for an hour and no one responds, he gets upset and gives up the call, saying: there is no benefit. This man remained a thousand years less fifty years, and yet only a few believed with him.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Then the flood seized them﴾ (...) Because the story is sometimes abridged, mentioning the cause and the effect without detail: sending and a long stay, and after that seizing. But it is a seizing for a cause, which is His saying: ﴿while they were wrongdoers﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then the flood seized them﴾. ﴿Seized them﴾ is more emphatic than His saying "then He drowned them." The seizing occurs in return for an action, so it is a recompense.

(﴿The flood﴾ meaning: abundant water that surged over them and overwhelmed them so they drowned). It surged over them from every side, and we seek refuge in Allah. Allah the Exalted mentioned the nature of this matter, saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth. And We caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ [al-Qamar 11-12]. Note ﴿the gates of heaven﴾: all the gates of heaven were opened. When the gates of heaven are opened, it will be like waterskins. ﴿With water pouring forth﴾ means descending with intensity and force. ﴿And We caused the earth to burst with springs﴾: the whole earth burst into springs, until Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the oven boiled over﴾ [Hud 40], which is the place of fire far from moisture. ﴿Boiled over﴾ means it began to gush forth in springs. What do you think? The water would, within hours, reach above the peaks of the mountains, and so it was, by the permission of Allah. It was so: the whole earth gushed forth springs, and the sky poured down mighty waters. ﴿And the waters met﴾, the water of the earth and the water of the sky, ﴿for a matter already decreed﴾. Who would be saved from this? It is related in a hadith: "If Allah were to save anyone, He would have saved the mother of the child": a woman with a child who, whenever the water reached her, climbed the mountain, and whenever it reached her again, she climbed, until she reached the summit of the mountain. When the water overtook her, she lifted her child above her so that she would drown before her son [narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3349) from the hadith of 'A'ishah]. But, we seek refuge in Allah, the mercy of Allah does not reach the disbelievers after they see the punishment: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir 85]. Anyway...

* Student: The real sky?

* The Shaykh: The sky that is above you; whatever is above you is a sky.

(﴿Then the flood seized them﴾ meaning: abundant water that surged over them and overwhelmed them so they drowned).

﴿And they were wrongdoers﴾: the clause ﴿and they were wrongdoers﴾ is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the pronoun in His saying ﴿seized them﴾. That is, while they were in a state of wrongdoing, meaning they persisted in injustice and did not believe, since only a small group believed with Noah.

(﴿فَأَنجَيْنَاهُ﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:15] i.e., Noah) from this great flood, ﴿وَأَصْحَابَ السَّفِينَةِ﴾ ("and the companions of the ship"). ﴿وَأَصْحَابَ﴾ (and the companions of): what is the object being conjoined? It is conjoined to the pronoun "him" (هاء) in ﴿أَنجَيْنَاهُ﴾; meaning: We also saved the companions of the ship, i.e., its people, (those who were with him in it), and they were the believers, Noah's family entirely except his disbelieving son, and the believers among his people. And likewise the animals: ﴿مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ [Hud 11:40] ("two of every pair"). Every creature that lives on the earth among the animals was carried in this ship, because (...) every thing on the earth; these are the companions of the ship, and they were saved.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ ("and We made it a sign for the worlds"): We made it a lesson for the worlds. In ﴿جَعَلْنَاهَا﴾, the pronoun refers either to the story (القِصَّة), or to the ship (السفينة).

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: It supports that it is the ship, since it refers to the nearest mentioned thing. And it supports the generality (that it is a lesson for all) that the lesson is not in the ship alone but in the ship and in the story too; since he remained this long period and only a few believed with him, and this great drowning occurred, for which there is no parallel as far as we know. So it is a sign for the worlds.

As for it being the ship: Allah the Exalted says: ﴿وَخَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مِثْلِهِ مَا يَرْكَبُونَ﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:42] ("and We created for them of its likeness that which they ride"). ﴿مِنْ مِثْلِهِ﴾ means: of the likeness of the laden ark in which Noah was saved, ﴿مَا يَرْكَبُونَ﴾. So Noah became the first to build ships, then people took it from him. Reflect on the wisdom in His saying: ﴿وَحَمَلْنَاهُ عَلَى ذَاتِ أَلْوَاحٍ وَدُسُرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar 54:13] ("and We carried him upon one of planks and nails"), and He did not say "We carried him upon the ship." Why? To draw attention to the materials that they call the raw materials in the making of a ship. What are they? The planks (الألواح) and the nails (الدُّسُر), meaning the nails; the meaning is that it is made of planks and nails, so that people would know this. This is the reality, everyone has known it, and the craft developed until it reached what it has reached now.

As for His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾, some scholars say: ﴿جَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ refers to the ship itself, specifically, and that this ship remained among the nations until the last of the nations, who are the first of this Ummah, reached it. It is said that parts of this ship remained existing until the first of this Ummah reached it on al-Judi, where it came to rest. But this is open to scrutiny.

The second view is that the pronoun in ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ refers to the ship in terms of its kind (باعتبار الجنس), not in terms of the individual (باعتبار الشخص). So the pronoun refers to it in terms of its kind, like His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ وَجَعَلْنَاهَا رُجُومًا لِلشَّيَاطِينِ﴾ [al-Mulk 67:5] ("And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps, and We made them missiles against the devils"), where ﴿جَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ means the meteors that come out of these lamps. And as in His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ (١٢) ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُطْفَةً﴾ [al-Mu'minun 23:12-13] ("And We certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a sperm-drop"). Does this pronoun in ﴿جَعَلْنَاهُ﴾ refer to man in terms of his kind or in terms of his individual?

* Student: In terms of his kind, because the first (man) was Adam...

* Shaykh: Do not give a reason (...). Who agrees or disagrees?

* Student: In terms of the kind.

* Shaykh: In terms of the kind, yes. It cannot be in terms of the individual, because it is not Adam; it is the one who is a drop in the wombs. Was Adam, who was created from an extract of clay, a drop in the wombs, in a firm resting place? No. But ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاهُ﴾ means man in terms of his kind. So the pronoun refers to man in terms of the kind, not in terms of the individual. Based on this, does His saying here, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا﴾, mean the ship in terms of its kind, or in terms of its individual? That is, the ship itself, or the kind of ship?

There are two opinions among the scholars. I told you: some scholars say that this ship remained, its individual remained until the last of the nations, this nation, reached it, and according to this ﴿جَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ means the very ship itself.

Others say: No, the ship of Noah had great ribs, it broke apart, and the winds, the sun and people destroyed it, and it went away. But ﴿جَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ means the ship in terms of its kind.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: (...). We are speaking about the ship; it is the one we are discussing. Yes.

* Student: We say perhaps (...).

* Shaykh: In any case, the matter has two opinions among the people of knowledge: either in terms of the individual, or in terms of the kind.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾: the intended meaning of "the worlds" (الْعَالَمِينَ) here is those after them among mankind, as the author said: (for those after them among people, if they disobey their messengers). This is from the author; it is as if he says: the pronoun in ﴿جَعَلْنَاهَا﴾ refers to the whole story, and that it is a lesson for the worlds: if they disobey their messengers, there will befall them the punishment that befell the people of Noah.

﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ (for those after them among people, if they disobey their messengers. And Noah lived after the flood sixty years). That makes forty years before the mission, and sixty years after the flood, a hundred years, and nine hundred and fifty: that is nine hundred and fifty years... but the author returned and said: (sixty years or more, until the people multiplied). That is, he did not affirm that only sixty years remained after the flood.

We say: there is no benefit for us in knowing how long he remained before the message, nor in knowing how long he remained after the flood; because what is important? What is important is the story.

Indeed, this one is the first of the messengers, peace be upon them, and yet he encountered from his people opposition, arrogance and rejection of his call, the like of which no prophet encountered; for we do not know that any prophet remained among his people for a thousand years minus fifty years except Noah. As for the popular proverb among people, which says: "May your life be the life of Shu'ayb" (عسى عُمْرك عُمْر شعيب), this is well known among us; I do not know, is it known among you? When they want to wish people long life, they say: "May your life be the life of Shu'ayb," thinking that the lifespan of Shu'ayb was the longest of lifespans. But this is not correct. Now, what has reached us from the Book of Allah, the Exalted, is that the longest-lived of people was Noah; this is what has reached us. So if they said: "May your life be the life of Noah," it would make sense. But "May your life be the life of Shu'ayb" (...).

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: I do not know whether they hold this assumption, or whether it is Shu'ayb, brother of Madyan.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: I do not know; Allah knows best.

In the story of Noah, Allah the Exalted says: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 26:105] ("The people of Noah denied the messengers"), and Allah says: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:14]. There is no plurality; Noah is one. What is its (wording) like?

* Student: In terms of the kind; meaning: they denied the Messenger, so they denied the messengers.
