People say that if the strongest iron and the most resistant iron were brought near its heat, it would turn to dust before reaching it because of the intensity of the heat. This is a known matter, because if you kindled a great fire from the most powerful fires of this world, would you find this heat in it from this distance? Never. Furthermore, this sun has a rising every day and a setting every day, because Allah subjected it in this way. Were it not so, the risings of winter and the risings of summer would not differ.

* Student: They say: if the sun descended by the measure of a mile, the earth would burn.
* Shaykh: No, they say: if the sun descended by the measure of a hair, it would burn.
* Student: Perhaps "milli."
* Shaykh: Perhaps.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, because the earthly envelope prevents this thing there.
* Student: If the earth were raised (...) if the earth ascended (...).
* Shaykh: By Allah, we do not know about this. In any case, there is no doubt that if it came close to the earth or moved away, the atmosphere would certainly change: if it approached the earth or moved away, it would change. Yet on the Day of Resurrection it will be, between it and people, at the measure of a mile, and the earth will not burn, and Allah is powerful over all things. We do not measure the conditions of the Hereafter by the conditions of this world. The most important thing for us is that it is subjected for our benefit: by it fruits ripen and by it years are known.

His saying: ﴿And the moon﴾, the moon is well known. Allah mentioned here the sun and the moon only because of their apparent benefits, since the stars and planets have no apparent benefits for us. Otherwise, Allah has subjected the sun, the moon, and all the stars for us, but these two are more manifest and clearer.

In His saying: ﴿He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾ there is evidence that it is they which move around the earth, travelling around the earth, contrary to those who say they do not travel over the earth, and that this alternation of night and day is due to the rotation of the earth itself.

Undoubtedly, whoever does not believe that they revolve around the earth is in great danger, and this may lead him to disbelief, because what we believe and hold is what Allah has informed us of: that it is the sun that revolves around the earth, and likewise the moon. ﴿And you would see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them on the left﴾ [al-Kahf 17]. Allah attributed all these four actions to the sun: ﴿rises﴾, ﴿inclines﴾, ﴿sets﴾, ﴿passes﴾.

Had the matter been as these conjecturers say, it would be the earth that inclines, and it is the earth that rises upon the sun and sets away from it. They have nothing but speculative matters, while the Qur'an's indication is apparent that it is the sun that revolves around the earth, and likewise the moon. The Prophet ﷺ, when the sun set, said to Abu Dharr: "Do you know where it goes?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7424) and Muslim (159), the wording being his, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari.]] He did not say: "Do you know where we go away from the sun?" Rather, the sun is what goes, what comes, what seeks permission, and what is permitted or prevented.

It is strange that this view contrary to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an has spread to people whose religion is not doubted; I mean, their religion is not in doubt, but the mirage deceived them and they were fooled. Our duty regarding these matters is to follow the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, until it becomes clear to us what contradicts this apparent meaning.

As for what the Qur'an indicates with certain indication, nothing can contradict it. The indication of the Qur'an is either apparent or explicit; the explicit is definitive in indication, and nothing can contradict it, while the apparent is speculative in indication. So we remain on this principle, we remain upon the apparent until it becomes clear to us by a definitive matter that its opposite holds; and then, as long as it is apparent, it may be interpreted.

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Do not say it like this. If you say it like this, they will take up the picks and axes against you, saying: "Are we crazy, Shaykh?"
* Student: By Allah, crazy.
* Shaykh: It is now prescribed for you in schools; a small child studies it and is nourished by it.
* Student: Praise be to Allah, I did not study it.
* Shaykh: Yes, praise be to Allah that Allah has saved you.
* Student: The matter of the revolving and stability of the sun or the moon (...) is definitive, and the matter of establishing the revolution of the earth is speculative.
* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, no, no. The fact that these things revolve around the earth: we now have three matters in reality. The establishment of the sun and moon, meaning their standing still, this contradicts the Qur'an.
The second: that the night and day occur due to the rotation of the earth, or due to the rotation of the sun and moon. This is contrary to the apparent meaning. The third thing: the rotation of the earth itself. The Qur'an contains nothing, neither apparent nor explicit, indicating that it rotates or does not rotate; there is no evidence.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, no, that is not correct, because it does not rotate in parts; it rotates as a whole. No, this is not correct. But regarding the matter of the earth's rotation, I say nothing about it. I say: Allah knows best. ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it shake with you﴾ [al-Nahl 15].

A speaker may say: His saying ﴿lest it shake with you﴾ indicates that there is movement, and the mountains were placed to balance this movement, because negating the more specific does not negate the more general. Yet still we say: what are we to us with this inquiry? If this were among the matters we are obliged to believe or to believe its negation, it would have been clarified in the Qur'an with utmost clarity, because Allah says: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾ [al-Nahl 89].

But the danger is that some refuse of ideas comes and takes control of our thinking, and then we accept it with acceptance and submission without returning to the Qur'an. This is the problem. For instance, if it were supposed now, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness, that this Qur'an were composed by a human and said: "The sun runs," and said: "He wraps the night over the day," it is known that "takwir" means "tadwir" (rotation), and that night and day come about because of what? Because of the sun. Then another book comes and says: "No, He makes the earth revolve so that night and day differ," we would say: these two books are contradictory, and preference must be sought. But if this is the speech of Allah, then no consideration is given to anything that contradicts it. This is the crux of the matter.

* Student: As long as the early generations (al-salaf) and the Messenger ﷺ did not explain (...), and the early generations did not mention it, why should we occupy ourselves with it and speak thus?
* Shaykh: No, better: we should not occupy ourselves with it. But as I told you at the beginning, if a person is tested, he must descend into the arena. The methods of the people of kalam in establishing creed: is this from the method of the early generations?
* Student: No.
* Shaykh: Good. Did the imams of Islam leave them to themselves? They engaged them in battle. If we are tested with a people who bring us into the arena, we must enter. For example, perhaps forty years ago people did not understand this matter, and it never occurred to them at all, except that people held to their innate beliefs that the sun rises and sets, and the moon rises and sets.
* Student: We refute them until they bring evidence.
* Shaykh: Yes, we refute them; not everything is refuted.
* Student: No, in the same rotation and in the same...
* Shaykh: We refute them in their saying that the alternation of night and day is due to the rotation of the earth, until they bring a definitive, clear proof, like the sun, which would be a proof for us in interpreting the apparent verses. Otherwise we will never accept it. Even if they all gathered, we would not accept it, because we know that all of them are conjectures, and the later ones transmit the words of the earlier ones exactly and in detail, which indicates that the later scholars are parrots: whenever something is spoken to them, they repeat what they heard.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: This is from the trial.
* Student: ﴿And you see the mountains, you think them motionless, while they pass like the passing of clouds﴾ [al-Naml 88]. This is evidence.
* Shaykh: Yes, they bring things that have no basis.

He said: ﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾. The subjection of the moon is also for the benefits and interests of the servants: ﴿And the moon, We have determined for it phases until it returns like the old dried palm stalk﴾ [Ya-Sin 39]. For what? Allah explained the wisdom in that: ﴿And He determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Yunus 5]. Thus by the variation of the moon's phases comes knowledge of the number of years and the reckoning, because the crescents are the natural universal timings. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say: they are timings for the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 189], in general. He also said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah 36]. These months are the lunar months which the Messenger ﷺ explained.

* Student: Some writers mentioned that people used to believe that the moon (...), as if they believed that a celestial animal lies in wait for the moon and hides it from the earth.
* Shaykh: By Allah, here in Najd we do not believe this. Perhaps this is what they believe there. Just as in some countries they believe that an eclipse is caused, meaning one of the creatures comes between it and the earth, and they go out with drums chanting: "O so-and-so! O so-and-so! Rescue the moon!" or something like that. I forgot what the one who told me the story said about it. The fish.

His saying: ﴿They will surely say: Allah﴾. The lam here is the answer to the oath. The first lam in ﴿And if you asked them﴾ precedes the oath, and this one falls in the answer to the oath.

His saying: ﴿Surely they will say﴾ (layaqulunna). Among you the grammarians will say: why was it built on damm although it is attached to the nun of emphasis? It is known that the imperfect, when attached to the nun of emphasis, is built on fath, and here it says ﴿layaqulunna﴾, so how do we answer?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What is in front of us now: the lam beside the nun.
* Student: Yes, but the nun of the verb is deleted (...) and the waw was deleted to avoid successive similar letters.
* Shaykh: No, but you answer me: the nun is directly attached to the verb. We say: it is required that the attachment be verbal and notional, and here the attachment is verbal, not notional. Therefore Ibn Malik says in the Alfiyyah:

............................. ∗∗∗ And they made the imperfect declinable if it is free
from the nun of emphasis directly attached ∗∗∗ .............................

Meaning: directly attached verbally and notionally, and from the nun of feminine plural. Is it clear? So we say: the nun is not directly attached to the verb notionally, because between it and the verb there intervened a noun and a letter: a noun, which is the waw, and a letter, the nun. The nun of the imperfect was deleted to avoid successive similar letters, which is a well-known grammatical argument, as you know. The waw is the waw of the subject, which was deleted to avoid the meeting of two sukun; because when the first nun was deleted to avoid successive similar letters, the second nun became doubled, and a doubled letter begins with a sukun, so it meets the silent waw, and then we delete the waw.

............................. ∗∗∗ And if it is soft, its deletion is deserved.

So we say: ﴿layaqulunna﴾. Was the nun of emphasis not directly attached to the verb verbally or notionally? It was not directly attached to the verb notionally.

* Student: Shaykh, its original form is (layaqulūna).
* Shaykh: Its original form is (layaqūlūnanna). This is its origin. The first nun was deleted to avoid successive similar letters, the second nun became doubled, and its first is silent, meeting the silent waw, so the waw was deleted, and it became ﴿layaqulunna﴾. He said: ﴿layaqulunna﴾, meaning: the questioned among the disbelievers.

﴿Allah﴾: The best thing is to say: ﴿Allah﴾ is the predicate of an omitted subject, estimated as (He is Allah). They acknowledge that the One who created them is Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾: He is Allah. They acknowledge that these things are not made by the gods, neither in creation nor in management. Look, glory be to Allah, the verse combines creation and management: it is an action in origination and an action in management; origination in His saying ﴿created the heavens and the earth﴾, and management in His saying ﴿and subjected the sun and the moon﴾, and He did not say "created."

Allah said: ﴿They will surely say: Allah﴾, so they acknowledge that the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the Subjector of the sun and the moon is Allah, not their idols. When they made this acknowledgment, they established the proof against them. Is it not so? Because whoever affirms lordship must affirm divinity, and whoever affirms divinity has affirmed lordship. Have you understood? They are mutually implicated: affirming lordship necessitates affirming divinity, even if affirmation of divinity does not occur; and affirming divinity necessitates affirming lordship. Which of them is prior? Affirmation of lordship is prior, because a person worships only a Lord whose names, attributes and actions he knows.

﴿They will surely say: Allah﴾: Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth, and He who subjected the sun and the moon.

Allah said: ﴿Then how are they turned away?﴾: they are diverted. "Anna" is an interrogative particle, and its purpose is rebuke: after they acknowledged this, how are they being turned away? The turning away is called ifk (falsehood) because it is diverting a thing from its reality. So ifk is diversion, just as when we turn speech away from reality it is called... if we turn speech away from reality, what is it called? It is called ifk. I tell you: "Zayd has arrived," and he has not arrived; this is ifk. So these were ufikū, that is, diverted from reality. His saying ﴿how are they turned away﴾ means: how are they diverted from His monotheism after their acknowledgment of that?

* Student: "Fa-anna yu'fakūn", what does it mean?
* Shaykh: How?

Allah said: (﴿Allah extends provision﴾: He widens it, ﴿for whom He wills of His servants﴾ as a trial, ﴿and restricts it﴾ means: He constricts it, ﴿for him﴾ after extending it, meaning: for whom He wills as a test.) ﴿Allah extends﴾: the meaning of yabsutu is yuwassi'u (widens). Provision means bounty.

His saying: ﴿of His servants﴾: is the intended meaning of "servants" here those who worship Him in the general sense, or in the specific sense?

* The students: In the general sense.
* Shaykh: In the general sense, encompassing believer and disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked. So Allah widens provision.

His saying: ﴿for whom He wills﴾: "man" here is a relative pronoun meaning "those who"; is it of the general relative nouns or the specific?

* Student: The general.

**Shaykh:** "al-'Ammah." His words "﴿لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾" mean: for whomever He wills to expand provision for. So the object of "﴿يَشَاءُ﴾" is omitted, and the context indicates it. There is a very important rule that we have already covered: whenever Allah ta'ala attaches something to His will, what is meant is a will based on wisdom, because all of Allah's actions and rulings, azza wa jall, are based on wisdom, whether we know it or not.

His words "﴿مِنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾": the author said "(امتحانًا) (as a test)," and at-Tadyiq (restriction) he said "(ابتلاءً) (as a trial)." Imtihan (testing) is in reality ibtila' (trial). Allah ta'ala said about Sulayman: ﴿هَذَا مِنْ فَضْلِ رَبِّي لِيَبْلُوَنِي أَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ﴾ ("This is from the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful").

His words "﴿لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾" and "﴿وَيَقْدِرُ﴾": yaqdiru here means yudayyiq (restricts). How do we know that "yaqdiru" here means "restricts"? And why did we not make "qudrah" here mean the ability to act?

**Student:** From His words "﴿يَبْسُطُ﴾."

**Shaykh:** From His words "﴿يَبْسُطُ﴾." Its contrast with expansion (basṭ) indicates that the meaning is restriction. From it is His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنْفِقْ﴾ ("And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend"). "﴿قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾" means: it was restricted for him.

His words "﴿يَقْدِرُ لَهُ﴾": the pronoun in "(له) (for him)" refers to "(من يشاء) (whoever He wills)," meaning: and He restricts for whoever He wills. Is the one for whom provision is expanded the same as the one for whom it is restricted? The apparent meaning of the author's words is that they are one and the same, which is why he said "and He restricts for him" after expansion. The reason is that the pronoun in "(له)" undoubtedly refers to "(من)" in His saying "﴿لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾." So it seems the author, may Allah have mercy on him, intended that it refers to him by his individual identity. But we say: there is nothing preventing it from referring to him by his category, not by his individual identity. So the pronoun refers to "(من يشاء) (whoever He wills)" by category, as in His saying: ﴿وَمَا يُعَمَّرُ مِنْ مُعَمَّرٍ وَلَا يُنْقَصُ مِنْ عُمُرِهِ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ﴾ ("No one is granted a lengthened life, nor is any of his life shortened, except that it is in a Book").

His words "﴿مِنْ عُمُرِهِ﴾": meaning of the one given a lengthened life? What is suitable of his life, i.e., of the one whose life is lengthened? If it is shortened, he would no longer be one whose life is lengthened. But what is meant by "his life" is by category, so it is the life of another person who is lengthened. Similar is when you say: "I gave this man a dirham and half of it." Half of what? Half of another dirham; it is not half of this dirham. You did not break the dirham. And if you had broken it and given him the whole, you would have given him all of it in two halves.

So what appears is that the pronoun in His saying "(له)" refers to "(من يشاء)," in terms of what? Category, not individual identity. So Allah ta'ala expands provision for this one and restricts it for that one. Just as He, glorified and exalted, expands it for this one at times and restricts it for him at other times. Do we not see now among the wealthy those who have become poor, and among the poor those who have become rich? So Allah, glorified and exalted, expands provision both by individual identity and by category. This expansion follows His knowledge and wisdom. That is why He said: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ("Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things"), and expansion and restriction are included in it. He, glorified and exalted, does not expand or restrict except with knowledge.

Then this knowledge is also followed by wisdom. He, glorified and exalted, makes wealthy the one for whom wealth is beneficial, and makes poor the one for whom poverty is beneficial. For this reason it came in the hadith: "Indeed among My servants is one who, if I made him wealthy, wealth would corrupt him, and indeed among My servants is one who, if I made him poor, poverty would corrupt him."[[Reported by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat (231) in similar wording, from the hadith of Anas.]] When Allah bestows favor upon the servant and is gracious to him, and makes his provision follow his welfare, great good results. And among the servants there is one who, if made wealthy, becomes corrupted. So in His saying "(ويقدر له) (and He restricts for him)," the pronoun refers to whom?

**Student:** To the author's words "(...)."

**Shaykh:** Yes, meaning: He expands for this one and restricts for that one.

**Student:** According to the author's words "(...)."

**Shaykh:** And His saying "﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾" means: all things, whether what He does or what the servants do; nothing of that is ever hidden from Him.

Some people said: "There is no general statement except that it has been specified, except His saying: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾." Is this correct? Some scholars—some of the usulis (scholars of legal theory)—said, when they spoke about al-'am wa al-khass (the general and the specific): "There is no general statement except that it has been specified, except His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾," because "﴿وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾" has no exception from it, neither the obligatory, nor the permissible, nor the impossible. Even the impossible, does He know it, glorified and exalted, or not? He knows it. And there is nothing in it that is specified at all. As for other general statements, they are specified, meaning that something is excluded from them, either by the indication of reason or by the indication of Shari'ah. But this statement is not correct. The correct view is that the basic principle regarding general statements is that they remain general. This is the basic principle for general statements. Yes, if they meant that specification is not conceivable in it, if they meant conception and assumption, this is possible. But if they meant the actual reality, then no.

The author said: "And among it is the locus of expansion and restriction." So He, glorified and exalted, knows that this one is deserving of having provision expanded for him, and that this one is deserving of having provision restricted for him.

**Student:** Shaykh Sulayman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shaykh Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab was asked about several issues.

**First issue:** Is it permissible for a Muslim to travel to the lands of the warring disbelievers (dar al-harb, abode of war) for the sake of trade, or not?

**Answer:** All praise is due to Allah. If he is able to manifest his religion and does not befriend the polytheists, it is permissible for him.

**Shaykh:** What, "wa la..?"

**Student:** "And does not befriend the polytheists, it is permissible for him." "Some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, such as Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and others among the Companions, traveled to the lands of the polytheists for trade, and the Prophet ﷺ did not object to that."[[Reported by Ibn Majah (3719) and Ahmad (26687) from the hadith of Umm Salamah.]] As related by Ahmad in his Musnad and others. But if he is not able to manifest his religion nor avoid befriending them, it is not permissible for him to travel to their lands, as the scholars explicitly stated. And by this are interpreted the hadiths that indicate that, or indicate the opposite. And by this are interpreted the hadiths that indicate the opposite.

**Shaykh:** What is the basic ruling? The basic principle?

**Student:** The basic principle is what I have transmitted, as the scholars explicitly stated, and by it is interpreted the hadiths that indicate the opposite, and by it is interpreted the hadiths that indicate that, like the hadith: "Whoever associates with the polytheist and lives with him, indeed he is one of them."[[Reported by Abu Dawud (2787) from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub.]] He combines the hadith of Abu Bakr's travel to the lands of the disbelievers and the Messenger ﷺ's approval of it, with the hadiths forbidding...

**Shaykh:** Perhaps, perhaps the correct view is the opposite.

**Student:** Yes, I will review it, God willing. Because Allah ta'ala obligated a person to act upon tawhid and imposed upon him enmity toward the polytheists, so whatever becomes a means and cause to abandon that is not permissible. And also, it may drag him to agreeing with them and pleasing them, as is the reality with many of the corrupt Muslims who travel to the lands of the polytheists. We seek Allah's refuge from that.

**Second issue:** Is it permissible for a person to sit...

**Shaykh:** The matter now is about the abode of war, you see, and there is a difference between the abode of war and the abode of covenant (dar al-'ahd). Its reasoning indicates generality, and his question...

**Student:** His question is about the abode of war, but this is permissible in the warring lands, permissible by way of...

**Shaykh:** No, let this be permissible. But if it is prohibited in the warring lands, is it prohibited in other than them? For example, if it is permissible...

**Student:** He permitted it in the warring lands.

**Shaykh:** He permitted it with the conditions you have, this is fine.

**Student:** If he permitted it in the warring lands, then he permitted it all the more in ordinary lands.

**Another student:** But the evidence for this does not indicate the warring lands...

**Shaykh:** And that it is general, his answer indicates generality, but the question is about the warring lands.

**Student:** Second issue: Is it permissible for a person to sit in the lands of the disbelievers while the symbols of disbelief are openly displayed, for the sake of trade?

The answer to this issue is the same as the previous one. There is no difference in this between the abode of war and the abode of peace (dar al-sulh). Every land where the Muslim cannot manifest his religion is not permissible for him to travel to.

**Third issue:** Is there a distinction between a short period, such as a month or two, and a long period?

**Answer:** There is no distinction between a short period and a long period. Every land in which one cannot manifest his religion nor avoid befriending the polytheists, it is not permissible for him to stay in it, not even for a single day, if he is able to leave it.

**Fourth issue:** Regarding the meaning of the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ﴾ ("Indeed, you would then be like them"), and the Prophet ﷺ's saying in the hadith: "Whoever associates with the polytheist and lives with him, indeed he is like him."[[Reported by Abu Dawud (2787) from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub.]]

**Answer:** The meaning of the verse is according to its apparent sense, which is that when a man hears the verses of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked, and he sits with the disbelieving mockers without being compelled, without denouncing them, and without standing up from them, until they plunge into speech other than it, then he is a disbeliever like them, even if he does not do their deed. Because that involves contentment with disbelief, and contentment with disbelief is disbelief. By this verse the scholars derived that one who is content with sin is like the one who commits it. If he claims that he hates that in his heart, it is not accepted from him, because judgment is based on the outward, and he has manifested disbelief, so he is a disbeliever.

**Shaykh:** He would be.

**Student:** So he is a disbeliever. For this reason, when apostasy occurred after the death of the Prophet ﷺ, and some people claimed that they disliked that, the Companions did not accept that from them. Rather, they considered them all apostates except one who denounced it with his tongue and his heart. Likewise His saying in the hadith: "Whoever associates with the polytheist and lives with him, indeed he is like him" is according to its apparent sense, which is that one who claims Islam, and is with the polytheists in gathering, support, and residence with them, such that the polytheists count him among them, is a disbeliever like them, even if he claims Islam, unless he manifests his religion and does not befriend the polytheists. For this reason, when some people who remained in Makkah after the Prophet ﷺ emigrated claimed Islam, but they remained in Makkah, the polytheists counted them among themselves, and they went out with them on the day of Badr, unwilling to go out with them, they were killed. Some Companions thought they were Muslims and said: "We have killed our brothers." So Allah ta'ala revealed about them: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ ("Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves") [an-Nisa': 97], the verse.[[Reported by al-Bukhari (4596) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] Al-Suddi and other exegetes said: "They were disbelievers, and Allah ta'ala did not excuse except the oppressed." End of quote.

I say: The answer to the hadith "Whoever associates with the polytheist and lives with him, indeed he is like him" has become clear, and that there is no difference between residence and temporary travel. But al-Shawkani transmitted regarding His saying: ﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾ ("O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast") [al-'Ankabut: 56].

**Shaykh:** From where did al-Shawkani transmit this?

**Student:** Al-Shawkani transmitted it in his tafsir. I am studying it, I am reviewing the references, but I abridge the pages. But al-Shawkani transmitted regarding His saying: ﴿يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ ("O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast, so worship Me alone") [al-'Ankabut: 56], that al-Zajjaj said: They were commanded to emigrate from the place where they cannot worship Allah. Likewise, it is obligatory upon one who is in a land where sins are committed and he cannot change that, to emigrate to where he can worship Allah as He deserves. I say—and I am the one saying it—there is something to examine in this.

**Shaykh:** Allah is the one sought for help!

**Student:** And Allah is the one sought for help.

**Shaykh:** If we acted by this (...) except the Companions.

**Student:** I said: There is something to examine in this.

**Shaykh:** Who mentioned "I said"?

**Student:** I mentioned it. Since the Prophet ﷺ mentioned the lowest level of denouncing evil and did not make emigration obligatory, rather it is obligatory to distance oneself from sitting with the people of evil. And delaying clarification beyond the time of need is impermissible. And the last statement may be the remainder of al-Zajjaj's speech, or a new statement from al-Shawkani, may Allah have mercy on them both. So the wording is problematic: is it from al-Zajjaj or from al-Shawkani? His saying: "Likewise, it is obligatory upon one who is in a land where sins are committed and he cannot change that, to emigrate."

Al-Qurtubi, regarding His saying: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ [an-Nisa': 97], in his transmission of a statement from Ibn al-'Arabi, said: The first: emigration, which is leaving the abode of war for the abode of Islam, and it was obligatory for the Prophet ﷺ...

**Shaykh:** Is it correct that the issue of practicing manifest sins, if you are compelled to remain with them? But if you are in your house where there is no sin, though in the markets there are sins, yet in your house there is no sin, and you only pass by them in passing, then I do not think any of the scholars says that emigration is obligatory. Yes, if it becomes that this place commands sins and you are compelled to remain in it, we say: you must leave. You must go and depart.

**Student:** And since you work there, O Shaykh, and since you work in (...), this where sins are open.

**Shaykh:** It is not permissible. For this reason we said: it is not permissible to take employment in banks. Even those who do not write usury, some of them say: "I do not write, I only serve them coffee and sweep for them and decorate for them." I say: But your presence in this place means contentment and acceptance. So for this it is not permissible.

**Student:** If I become a clerk, I will write, and the clerks with me are all shaved and smoke tobacco.[[Tatan: tobacco.]]

**Shaykh:** No, regarding the matter of smoking tobacco, yes, because he is committing a sin in front of you.

**Student:** And the beard too.

**Shaykh:** As for the beard, it is not that its shaving is in front of me now; this is the trace of shaving. The trace of shaving is not my concern. But the discussion is about smoking tobacco, if it is not possible (...), troubles.

**Student:** The first—in his transmission of Ibn al-'Arabi's statement—the first: emigration, which is leaving the abode of war for the abode of Islam, and it was obligatory for the Prophet ﷺ. This emigration remains until the Day of Resurrection, but the destination toward it wherever it is has ceased—with a fatha on the last letter—because when a Muslim remains in the abode of war, he disobeys.

The second: leaving the land of innovation, said Ibn al-Qasim: I heard Malik say: "It is not lawful for anyone to reside in a land where the predecessors are reviled."  Ibn al-'Arabi said: This is correct, for if you cannot change the evil, then withdraw from it: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ الَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِي آيَاتِنَا فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ ("And when you see those who engage in vain discourse concerning Our verses, turn away from them until they enter into another conversation... the wrongdoers") [al-An'am: 68].

Is this statement of Ibn al-'Arabi correct?

**Shaykh:** Correct, just as we said: if it becomes that you are compelled to remain with them in the same place, you must leave. But if it becomes that everyone is in his house, or he is not (...).

**Student:** He said: The third: leaving a land where the unlawful has dominated, for seeking the lawful is an obligation upon every Muslim.

**Shaykh:** Like what?

**Student:** If they deal only in usury, meaning all the people.

**Shaykh:** All the people?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 29, verse 59–62 (part 5 of 6):

* The student: This is an actual situation. I heard a fatwa from some shaykhs in my country, where the whole country deals in riba, and he says to him: what do you do? I mean, the work would be what, would it be according to need or not according to need? Nearly all the banks now deal abroad.
* The Shaykh: All banks, no harm. But do all people run banks? There are, for example, restaurants, there are grocery shops, there are clothing merchants.
* The student: The original funds are, in fact, the state's funds in the banks.
* The Shaykh: In any case (...) as the jurists say (...).
* The student: A question: is it obligatory for him to denounce the wrong and to declare it false? Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said in his tafsir, regarding the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent pattern in Ibrahim and those with him﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 4]: there has been for you, O believers, an excellent example in Ibrahim, the friend of the All-Merciful, whom you should follow, and those with him from the prophets of Allah. ﴿When they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah"﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 4]: when they said to their people, who disbelieved in Allah and worshipped the taghut: O people, indeed we are free of you and of those you worship besides Allah, of the gods and rivals. ﴿We have disbelieved in you﴾: so we denounced the disbelief you were upon, and we rejected your worship of what you worship besides Allah. ﴿And there has started between us and you enmity and hatred forever﴾: enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever, because of your disbelief in Allah, ﴿until you believe in Allah alone﴾: there is no reconciliation between us and no leniency until you affirm Allah alone, so that you single Him out and dedicate worship to Him.
I say: Allah has followed this with His saying, glorified is He: ﴿There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away—indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 6]. The apparent meaning of this is that it is obligatory.
* The Shaykh: The statement of disavowal of the disbelievers is obligatory.
* The student: And His saying: ﴿We have disbelieved in you, and there has started between us and you enmity and hatred forever﴾.
* The Shaykh: Yes, yes, we say to him: no.
* The student: The verse's apparent and explicit meaning is that this is obligatory.
* The Shaykh: It is obligatory that we say this, but is it, for example, if we are in a position in some country, can we say these words?
* The student: One must emigrate, because it is obligatory to manifest the religion. Al-Shawkani said, on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious﴾ (the verse), he said: ﴿Indeed My earth is spacious﴾: if you are in constriction in Makkah from manifesting faith and from the plotting of the disbelievers, then go out so that worship of Me becomes easy for you and facilitated for you, and [away] from the plotting of the disbelievers.
* The Shaykh: Yes, they plot against you.
* The student: Yes. And Shaykh Abd al-Rahman ibn Hasan said, in the context of his explanation of the inclusion of two matters in the core and foundation of religion, he said: Then he said, may Allah have mercy on him: The apparent meaning is that the statement is explicit (...) and he did not declare them disbelievers. This type also has not brought what la ilaha illa Allah indicates of negating shirk, and what it necessitates of declaring disbelieving whoever does it after clarification, by consensus. It is the content of Surah al-Ikhlas, and ﴿Say, O disbelievers﴾ [al-Kafirun 1], and His saying in the verse of al-Mumtahanah: ﴿We have disbelieved in you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 4]. Whoever does not declare disbelief upon those whom the Qur'an declared disbelievers has opposed what the messengers brought of tawhid and what it requires.
Then he, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (Among them—and it is the most dangerous of the types—is one who acts upon tawhid but does not know its worth, does not hate those who abandon it, and does not declare them disbelievers.)
His saying, may Allah have mercy on him: (and it is the most dangerous of the types), is because whoever does not know the measure of what he acts upon, and has not brought what makes his tawhid valid of the heavy conditions that are indispensable, does not know that tawhid requires negating shirk and disavowing it, opposing its people and declaring them disbelievers, when the proof has been established against them. This person may be deceived by his own condition, while he has not brought the matters that the words of sincerity indicate, in negation and affirmation. End.
Shaykh Sulayman ibn Abd Allah ibn Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab was asked: Is allying with the disbelievers out of partisanship—because the apparent wording of the Shaykh indicates that it is obligatory to oppose them and to be harsh in that, and to openly insult their religion and revile their gods; this is the apparent meaning of the statement—then he said: Shaykh Sulayman ibn Abd Allah ibn Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab was asked: Is allying with the disbelievers out of worldly partisanship an allegiance of hypocrisy, or do they become disbelievers? And if he cannot utter their disbelief and insult them, what is his ruling? And if you know this from a person, what is obligatory upon you?
He answered: If the alliance is together with residing in their lands and going out with them in their fighting and the like, then the one who does it is judged a disbeliever, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever among you allies with them is indeed one of them﴾ [al-Ma'idah 51]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they enter into a conversation other than it; indeed, you would then be like them﴾ [al-Nisa' 140]. And the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever associates with the polytheists and dwells with them, indeed he is like them" [Abu Dawud (2787), from the hadith of Samurah ibn Jundub]. And he said: "I am free of every Muslim who dwells among the polytheists" [Abu Dawud (2645), and al-Tirmidhi (1604), from the hadith of Jarir ibn Abd Allah]. Both were narrated by Abu Dawud.
And if the alliance is in the lands of Islam—I searched in Ibn al-Qayyim, perhaps I find a statement on this; I searched in Ibn al-Qayyim's Mukhtasar Tahdhib al-Sunan—and he said: If the alliance is in the lands of Islam, when they come to them and the like, then this is a sinner, guilty, exposed to the threat. And if their alliance is for the sake of their religion (thus in the original), it is obligatory upon us to discipline with boycott and correction and the like of what deters the likes of him. I think he means for the sake of encouraging them toward the religion.
* The Shaykh: Not for the sake of their religion.
* The student: Now it will come after the statement about them, because it is disbelief; allying with them for the sake of their religion is disbelief.
* The Shaykh: No, for the sake of their religion, or their worldly life?
* The student: Or perhaps their worldly life, yes, correct, perhaps their worldly life. But this and that (...). And if the alliance is for the sake of their religion, then he is like them, and whoever loves a people is gathered with them. But let the questioner reflect on his saying: worldly partisanship. This is not possible except to convey love into their hearts; otherwise, if he hated them for Allah's sake and opposed them, the thing most pleasing to their eyes would be what displeases them, as Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said:
Do you love the enemies of the Beloved, while claiming a love for Him that is not possible?
As for the questioner's saying: If he cannot from himself utter their disbelief and insult them? The answer: it is not free of this: either he is doubtful about their disbelief or ignorant of it, or it is said: he acknowledges that they and their likes are disbelievers, but he cannot confront them and declare them disbelievers, or he says: others are disbelievers, I do not say they are disbelievers. If he is doubtful about their disbelief or ignorant of their disbelief, the proofs from the Book and the Sunnah are made clear to him for their disbelief.
If he doubts that and hesitates, then he is a disbeliever by the consensus of the scholars, since whoever doubts the disbelief of the disbelievers is a disbeliever. And if he acknowledges their disbelief but cannot confront them by declaring them disbelievers, then he is a flatterer (mudahin), and he falls under His saying: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam 9], and he has the ruling of those like him among the people of sins.
* The Shaykh: If he remains among them?
* A student: If he remains among them and flatters them by silence, saying: I fear they will expel us. And if he says: I say others are disbelievers, I do not say they are disbelievers, then this is a judgment by him of their being Muslims, since there is no intermediary between disbelief and Islam. If they are not disbelievers, then they are Muslims. Then whoever names disbelief as Islam, or names the disbelievers as Muslims, is a disbeliever, so this one is a disbeliever.
As for his saying: If you know this from a person, what is obligatory upon you? The answer: it is obligatory upon you to advise him, call him to Allah the Exalted, and make him know the ugliness of what he has committed. If he repents, this is what is sought. If he persists and is obstinate, then he has the ruling of what he committed: if it is disbelief, then he is a disbeliever; if it is disobedience or sin, then he is a sinner, guilty. It is obligatory to denounce him, discipline him, boycott him and distance him until he repents. The Prophet ﷺ boycotted those who stayed behind from a single battle, and forbade speaking to them and greeting them. So how about one who allies with the disbelievers and shows them affection? End.
I say: It becomes clear from this that denouncing them and clarifying their misguidance is obligatory upon whoever goes to their lands, either as disbelief if he loves them and allies with them, or if he does not believe in their disbelief, even if he fears they will expel him, then he is sinful and exposed to the threat. The Shaykh Sulayman has mentioned this.
* The Shaykh: Is this last answer from his statement?
* The student: This is from my own statement.
* The Shaykh: No, the last answer?
* The student: Yes, the last answer is from his statement, but I said..
* The Shaykh: No, leave what you said from your own words.
* The student: But the first is all from his answer.
* The Shaykh: The answer of whom?
* The student: The answer of Sulayman ibn Abd Allah ibn Shaykh Muhammad. I am only transmitting; the first part is transmitted.
* The Shaykh: (...).
* The student: Then he said: Shaykh Sulayman ibn Abd Allah ibn Shaykh Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab mentioned matters in which he said: What is understood from what we have mentioned of the Book, the Sunnah, and the reports from the early generations are matters; whoever does them enters into those verses and exposes himself to the threat of being touched by the Fire. We seek refuge in Allah from what necessitates His anger and His painful punishment. We mention from them the following: affection and special love, flattering them and courting them, obeying them in what they say and announce, placing them ahead in sitting or entering before the rulers of Islam, consulting them in matters, sitting with them, visiting them and entering upon them.
"The mother of Asma came to her while she was a disbeliever, and the Messenger said: 'Maintain ties with your mother'" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2620), and Muslim (1003/50), from the hadith of Asma bint Abi Bakr]. So a person believes its repetition.
* The Shaykh: The apparent meaning is that sitting with them is a kindness toward them, because this is kinship, and kinship has a right even if she is a disbeliever.
* A student: And the kindness: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah 8].
* The Shaykh: Yes, sitting leads to companionship and familiarity.
* A student: And visiting them means repeated visits, entering upon them, showing them a cheerful face and warmth, assisting them in their affairs even with a little, such as sharpening the pen and bringing the inkwell closer so they may write their injustice.
* The Shaykh: So they may write their injustice.
* A student: Keeping company with them and living with them, approving of their deeds, imitating them, dressing in their fashion, mentioning what contains glorification of them, such as calling them lords, dwelling with them in their lands.
Shaykh Abd al-Aziz ibn Baz, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked about the ruling on travelling to the lands of disbelievers for learning. This is from (...).
He answered: It is not permissible except with three conditions: that the Muslims have a pressing need for this knowledge; that this knowledge is not found in the lands of the Muslims; and the ability to manifest his religion. I say: to these two is added what Shaykh Sulayman ibn Abd Allah mentioned of the condition of safety from their alliance and affection. I think it is included in the third matter, the ability to manifest the religion, which includes safety. Also added is what one of the scholars stipulated, namely that he be knowledgeable of his creed and able to refute the doubts of the enemies of Allah and His Messenger. This, and Allah knows best.
* The Shaykh: And is he secure for himself, meaning does he have strength from religion so that he is safe from desires? We mentioned yesterday three cases: the need, and the second: that he has knowledge by which he repels doubts, and has religion by which he repels desires.
* A student: He has knowledge of his creed.
* * *
* The Shaykh: ﴿Those who are patient and upon their Lord rely﴾ [al-Ankabut 59].
* From this verse is derived: the virtue of patience, since Allah praised the patient: ﴿those who are patient﴾.
* And among its benefits also: the obligation of singling out Allah, glorified and exalted, for reliance and trust, by His saying: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.
* And among them: it is fitting for the patient person to rely on his Lord in his patience, by His saying: ﴿those who are patient and upon their Lord rely﴾. The benefit of relying upon his Lord in his patience: first, steadfastness upon that, since Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [al-Talaq 3]. The second benefit: that his patience becomes an act of worship, because some people are patient and endure with the restraint of the poet's saying:
My endurance before the mockers, that I show them I do not waver before the turns of time.
This patience, there is no doubt, is a good character, but it is not rewarded. So we say: what? That patience accompanied by reliance upon Allah, glorified and exalted, is what carries the reward and the recompense.
* And from the benefits of the verse: the sufficiency of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since one relies only upon One who is sufficient; whoever is not sufficient is not fit to be relied upon.
* And from its benefits: the affirmation of lordship, by His saying: ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.
Then Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision; Allah provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-Ankabut 60].
* From the benefits of the verse: guidance to reflect upon the creatures of Allah, since Allah says: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾, so that we reflect upon these creatures that do not carry their provision.
* And among its benefits: that it includes several attributes of Allah. Among them: perfection of power, since He creates these small creatures that do not carry their provision, and creates great creatures that earn their provision.
* And also among its benefits: among the attributes derived from it is the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and among them His knowledge, and among them His mercy, and among them His encompassing of everything, since these small creatures that do not carry their provision, He knows them and provides for them.
And His saying: ﴿He provides for it and for you, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.
* A student: And among them (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, we have said it. Did we not mention it first?
* And among its benefits: the affirmation of the two names (All-Hearing) (All-Knowing) and what they include of attributes.
Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?" they would surely say, "Allah"﴾, and so on to the end [al-Ankabut: 61].
* In this verse are benefits: establishing the proof against the opponent until he submits and acknowledges.
* And among them: rebuking the polytheists regarding Allah in their worship, since they acknowledge His lordship and then deny His divinity; and it is from reason that whoever acknowledges lordship acknowledges divinity.
* And among them: affirmation of the creation of the heavens and the earth, and that the One who created them is Allah.
* And among them also: that the management of the universe belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and subjected the sun and the moon﴾.
* And among them: the mercy of Allah, exalted, toward His creation, since He subjected the sun and the moon for them.
* And among them: that the polytheists acknowledge lordship.

Among its benefits: acknowledging Allah's lordship (rububiyyah) is not sufficient for tawhid (monotheism in worship). From this point, and from what follows from it, we learn the falsity of the interpretation of ilah (deity) as "the one able to create (ikhtira')." The theologians (mutakallimun) define ilah as the one able to create. If they define ilah this way, their concept of tawhid does not differ from the tawhid of the polytheists. We say: ilah is the one truly worthy of worship, this true ilah who is worshipped in truth. Likewise, what is worshipped falsely is also called ilah, because it is worshipped, but its divinity is false.

Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge of the future, based on His saying ﴿They will surely say, "Allah"﴾. This is a report about a future matter, and there is no doubt that it occurs as Allah reported. I think we have mentioned the foolishness of these polytheists?

Student: Yes.

Shaykh: Good. ﴿So how are they deluded?﴾

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-'Ankabut 62]

Among the benefits of the verse: provision is in the hand of Allah. Since this is so, it is He from whom provision is to be sought.

Among its benefits: affirming qadar (divine decree) does not mean abandoning the means (asbab). Here Allah shows that extending and restricting provision is in His hand, yet He says: ﴿It is He who made the earth docile for you, so walk through its regions and eat of His provision﴾ [al-Mulk 15]. He did not say: "Sleep on your beds and provision will come to you." He said: ﴿so walk through its regions and eat of His provision﴾. So qadar does not negate doing the means, because provision may be decreed for you through this means. Likewise, entering Paradise and being saved from the Fire: does it not have a means? Yes. If you do not do it, it does not happen. Similarly, if you do not work for provision, what is decreed for you does not come to you.

Among its benefits: the affirmation of Allah's perfect disposal (kamal al-tasarruf), the Exalted: ﴿He extends provision to whom He wills and restricts﴾ [al-'Ankabut 62]. He gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips sovereignty from whom He wills, grants honour to whom He wills and humiliates whom He wills. He, glorified and exalted, has absolute disposal over His creation.

Among its benefits: the affirmation of will (mashi'ah), based on His saying ﴿for whom He wills﴾. Now we ask: does will relate to what He loves and what He dislikes, or only to what He loves? The Muslims agree on their saying: "What Allah wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur." Now, does volition (irada) relate to what He loves and what He dislikes, or only to what He loves?

Student: (...) the legislative (shar'iyyah).

Shaykh: Yes. There is a distinction: the legislative will (irada shar'iyyah) relates only to what He loves, and the universal will (irada kawniyyah) relates to what He loves and what He does not love, because it is synonymous with will (mashi'ah).

Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-'Ankabut 62], and that it is general over everything. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ Does it include the small and the great, and what relates to His action and what relates to the actions of His servants? If He knows the actions of His servants, it necessarily follows that He decrees them, because if He knows something, it cannot occur contrary to what He knows, and then He is its decreer. For this reason al-Shafi'i, in his debate with those Mu'tazilah who were Qadariyyah, said: "Argue with them using knowledge. If they deny it, they disbelieve; if they affirm it, they are refuted." This is correct. This is a firm and sound proof.

Among its benefits, from the verse: Allah's favour in provision, whether it is decreed (muqaddar) or extended (mabsut). Or, more precisely: whether it is maqdur or mabsut, because [the word] is from the triliteral (al-thulathi) and not from the quadriliteral (al-ruba'i).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 29, verse 63–67 (part 1 of 4):

His saying, "And if you asked them, 'Who sends down water from the sky and thereby revives the earth after its death?'" The "lam" here is the lam of oath, and the answer to the oath is: "they will surely say, 'Allah'" [al-Ankabut 63]. "And if you asked them, 'Who sends down from the sky...'" — "man" (مَن) here is a relative pronoun in the nominative as subject (mubtada'), its relative clause (silah) is the verb "nazzala", and the answer to the oath is "they will surely say, 'Allah'". Is this i'rab correct or not?
* Students: No, it is wrong.
* The Shaykh: It is wrong. "Man" (مَن) is an interrogative pronoun, because it occurs after the question: "And if you asked them, 'Who sent down...'" On this basis, "man" is the subject (mubtada'), and "nazzala" with its clause is the predicate of the subject. His saying "man nazzala" is with the doubled "zay" (nazzala, intensive form). In some verses it is "anzala min as-sama'" [al-An'am 99]. The difference between "nazzala" and "anzala" is that "nazzala" indicates that a thing descends gradually, bit by bit, as Allah the Exalted said about the Qur'an: "And [it is] a Qur'an which We have separated [in revelation] that you might recite it to the people over a long period, and We have sent it down in stages" [al-Isra' 106].
And His saying, "nazzala min as-sama'" — because descent occurs from above. The meaning of "as-sama'" (the sky) here is "the height," not the protected ceiling, as evidenced by His saying: "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ship which runs through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah sends down from the sky of water, and gives life thereby to the earth after its death... and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth" [al-Baqarah 164], and rain descends from the clouds: "Do you not see that Allah drives the clouds, then joins them, then makes them into a heap, and you see the rain emerge from within them" [al-Nur 43]. Thus we know that the meaning of "as-sama'" here is what? "The height." Everything that is above you is "sama'," because it derives from (sama, yasmu), meaning it rose and was elevated.
And His saying, "min as-sama' ma'an" — the wisdom in its descent from the sky is that when it descends from above, it covers what is below and what is high; if it flowed from the earth, it would not reach the high places before it destroyed what is below. But by the wisdom of Allah, it descends from above.
He said, "ma'an fa-ahya bihi al-ard" — the "fa" here indicates sequence and immediacy, but when it connects to a clause, it also indicates causation together with sequence and immediacy. This differs from when it precedes a noun, in which case it does not indicate causation. You say: "Zayd stood up, then 'Amr," which does not mean that Zayd's standing was the cause of 'Amr's standing, but that 'Amr's standing came after Zayd's standing. When it connects to a verb, however, it generally indicates sequence with causation. Accordingly, His saying "fa-ahya bihi al-ard" means that the water is the cause of the earth's revival. Now, His saying "fa-ahya bihi," does the earth come to life immediately or later?
* Students: Later.
* The Shaykh: Later. But since the cause is effective, the effect follows it immediately, like His saying: "Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?" [al-Hajj 63]. The earth does not become green merely by the water descending at night, but this is a necessitating cause. Since it is a necessitating cause, it is as if the effect exists at once. They said: Among this is their saying: "So-and-so married, and a child was born to him," although this is weaker than what we have here. But when he says "a child was born to him," we know with certainty that he was not begotten the night of his marriage or not? There is no difficulty in this; marriage is the cause of birth, and the sequence follows it. It is not necessary that it be immediate, but when the cause is necessitating and inevitable, the effect is as if it follows the cause directly.
And His saying: "fa-ahya bihi al-ard min ba'di mawtiha" — "ahya" (revive) and "mawt" (death) are applied to inanimate matter. So does it live and die or not? Inanimate matter lives and dies, and everything's life and death is according to its nature. Do not think that life and death are attributed only to what can move. Concerning these idols, Allah says: "And those whom they invoke besides Allah create nothing, while they are created. [They are] dead, not alive" [al-Nahl 20–21]. "Dead, not alive." So everything that has no movement and no growth can be called dead, even if it is something life does not inhabit.
And His saying: "ahya bihi al-ard min ba'di mawtiha" — is the meaning of "the earth" here the vegetation, or is it the earth itself? It has been said: the meaning is the earth itself, and by the mixing of water into it, it becomes living, and by its drying it becomes dead. It has also been said: the meaning is what is upon it of grass, crops and the like, i.e., the vegetation, and that the earth is not truly "earth" in the sense of being beneficial to people except through the vegetation above it, so its life and death are the life and death of its vegetation.
And His saying, the Exalted: "they will surely say, 'Allah'" — we say about it what has preceded: the lam occurs in the answer to the oath, and "yaqulunna" originally was "yaqulunanna." Have you seen? The grammarians said: the first nun was deleted because of the succession of similar sounds. Why do we not say: one of the two nuns of the emphatic nun was deleted? They said: because the emphatic nun was introduced for a purpose, which is emphasis, while the nun of the raf' (nominative ending) is always deleted in the case of the nasb (accusative), the jazm (jussive), the takhfif (lightening), and the like, so it was more appropriate for deletion. Thus we deleted the nun of raf' because of the succession of similar sounds. What is the reason for the deletion of the waw? Because of the meeting of two sukun (unvocalized letters), since the doubled emphatic nun consists of two letters, the first of which is unvocalized. When it is unvocalized, the weak letter before it, the soft vowel letter, is deleted, as Ibn Malik said:
"... and if it is a soft letter, its deletion is required."
And His saying, "Allah": we say it is the predicate of a deleted subject, or a subject whose predicate is deleted.
* A student: The reason for (...).
* The Shaykh: Allah knows best. We do not know how they say that mixing water with it is life. They say that this is a life appropriate to it. In truth, as I said a little while ago, life and death in vegetation are more evident, because it is the place of benefit. Perhaps one may cite as evidence His saying: "Or like one who passed by a town, while it was fallen upon its roofs. He said, 'How will Allah revive this after its death?'" [al-Baqarah 259]. The thing that is fallen upon its roofs is the vegetation or the earth? The vegetation. So "How will Allah revive this after its death" attributes death to the vegetation. This means that this supports the view that the revival of the earth and its vegetation means the revival of its vegetation and its death.
* A student: His saying, the Exalted: "You see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells" [Fussilat 39].
* The Shaykh: Yes. Some scholars said: the earth itself stirs, and it swells, that is, with the water it rises. This is the matter in it, but the apparent view, and Allah knows best, is that the closer opinion is that the meaning is the vegetation.
His saying: "They will surely say, 'Allah.' Say: 'Praise be to Allah.'" "Say: 'Praise be to Allah'" — He did not say here "How are they turned away?" There He said: "How are they deluded?" (fa-anna yu'fakun), because the indication of creation and governance for lordship, which necessitates acknowledgment of divinity, is evident. Here He said: "Say: Praise be to Allah," because their acknowledgment of the first and the second, and that the whole matter is in Allah's hand, necessitates not merely that Allah exists, but that Allah deserves to be praised. For this reason He said: "Say: Praise be to Allah." The proof has been established against you, the clear evidence has stood against you, and the perfection of Allah the Mighty and Majestic has become manifest. Do you understand? The first contains negation (takhliyah), the second contains affirmation (tahliyah), the affirmation of Allah's perfection. That is, "Praise be to Allah" for the establishment of the clear evidence against you and the manifestness and clarity of the proof.
As for the author's saying, "How then do they associate partners with Him?", he brought it in the manner of His saying in the first verse, "How are they deluded?" But in my view, the second verse contains the establishment of proof on another matter which they deny, namely the Resurrection, for they deny it. The reality of the matter is that one who denies the Resurrection will associate partners with Allah and will do whatever he wishes, because the denier of the Resurrection believes there is no reward and no reckoning, and whoever believes so, will he act? He does not act. For this reason, as you see, Allah the Exalted always combines in the Qur'an belief in Him with belief in the Last Day; He always combines them, because belief in the Last Day is what drives a person to action, for whoever does not believe there is a recompense, how will he act? What appears to me is that the second verse was brought to oblige them to acknowledge the Resurrection.
* A student: Some verses: "So He revives thereby the earth after its death" [al-Baqarah 164].
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, "after its death." Yes. The benefit: this revival may be close to the death of the earth, meaning that rain descends close to the drought, and sometimes it is delayed, so "min" (from/after) indicates the delay.
He said: "Say: Praise be to Allah," for the establishment of the proof against you. Now, "al-hamdu lillah" (praise belongs to Allah): what is praise (hamd)? Is it commendation? Most people say: it is commendation for good qualities. This is not correct, for commendation (thana') is other than praise (hamd). This is shown by the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, indeed by the saying of Allah, that commendation is other than praise in the sacred hadith, the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, that Allah, glorified and exalted, said: "I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves. When he says: 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds' [al-Fatihah 2], He says: My servant has praised Me. When he says: 'The Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful' [al-Fatihah 3], He says: My servant has commended Me. When he says: 'Master of the Day of Judgment' [al-Fatihah 4], He says: My servant has glorified Me." [Related by Muslim (395/38) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] This is clear evidence that commendation is other than praise, otherwise it would be repetition. Also, the meaning requires it, for "thana'" derives from "thaniyah," meaning return, for when you bend a staff, its end returns to its end. From it also comes the word "ithnan" (two), meaning one and one, in which there is return. The point is that "hamd" cannot be correctly explained as "thana'." So what is it? We say: it is describing the praised one with perfection, but we add also: together with love and magnification, so that flattery (madh) is excluded, for flattery is describing the one praised with perfection, but it may be out of love and magnification, or it may be out of fear and not love. This man who stood before an oppressive, tyrannical king and said: "You are the noble king, the benevolent, just one who wrongs no one" — is this flattery or not? It is flattery, but out of love and magnification? Not at all; it is a lie. So we say: praise (hamd) is describing the praised one with perfection together with love and magnification. Further, it is also distinguished from flattery in that flattery may conform to reality or may not, while praise must necessarily conform to reality.
He said: And His saying, "al-hamdu lillah": the scholars say that the "al" in "al-hamd" is for comprehensiveness (istighraq), so all praises belong to Allah. The lam in His saying "lillah," is it the lam of ownership or of its like? Ibn Malik says:
"And the lam is for ownership and its like..."
* A student: Its like.
* The Shaykh: Its like. So praise is due to Allah and specific to Allah, and what is meant is complete praise. As for mere praise, it is not specific to Allah; a person may be praised for one quality according to the measure of that quality, but complete and comprehensive praise belongs to Allah alone and is specific to Allah alone.
"Say: Praise be to Allah, but most of them do not know" — they do not realize their contradiction in this. Is "bal" here for transitional (intiqali) or for nullifying (ibtali) retraction?
* A student: Transitional.
* The Shaykh: Transitional. That is: after the matter has been established and the proof has stood, and the Creator has become worthy of commendation or praise, at that point it is correct to record ignorance against them, which is His saying: "But most of them do not reason." Most of these do not reason, meaning that they have such foolishness as is evident, for if they had intellects, their acknowledgment of what they acknowledged would have obliged them to acknowledge what they denied, or not? Yes, if they had genuine, rightly-guided intellects, their acknowledgment of what they acknowledged would have obliged them to acknowledge what they denied. They acknowledged that the One who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon is Allah, and that the One who sent down water from the sky and thereby revived the earth after its death is Allah. So where is intellect, while you deny the Resurrection and associate partners with the Creator?! Here there is no intellect.
From here we derive that those who claim they are the people of intellect, yet deny some of the attributes of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, arguing that intellect does not affirm them, we derive from this that they do not have intellect, for intellect obliges them to acknowledge what they denied, just as they acknowledged what they acknowledged.
For example — we will strike only two examples: the Ash'aris, and the discussion is with them and with whoever else, a fortiori, say: "We affirm for Allah will (irada), and we deny mercy (rahmah); Allah has no mercy." Why, O people? They say: "Yes, because will is indicated by reason, and mercy, reason has shown its invalidity." Look at what they say: "Reason has not indicated it; reason has shown its invalidity."
Now, explain: they say, "Will is indicated by reason through specification (takhsis): the specification of the sky being sky, the earth being earth, man being human, the donkey being an animal, and the like, i.e., a non-speaking animal. This indicates what? It indicates will: He willed the donkey to be a donkey, so it was a donkey; and He willed man to be a human, so he was a human; and He willed the sky to be sky, so it was sky," and so on.
Is this an indispensable proof for will? A clear proof, or not clear? Clear. Now mercy? They say: reason has shown its denial, why? They say: because mercy is softness and tenderness, and Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, is not described by softness and tenderness.
We said to them: You have argued from reality to will; we argue against you from reality to mercy, and the indication of reality for mercy is greater than the indication of reality for will. If you were to say to a common person, "What is your rational proof for will?" — by Allah, I do not know. Does the common person perceive that specification is evidence for will?
* A student: No.
* The Shaykh: Good. But if you say to the common person: Allah's sending down rain after drought so that the earth becomes fertile, and Allah's provision of wealth to the poor, so that he becomes rich after poverty, does this not indicate that Allah is merciful or not? What does he say? He says: yes. So the indication of the reality of the countless blessings of Allah for the mercy of Allah is more eloquent than the indication of specification for will. Is it clear? This is very clear.
Therefore, in reality, if they had intellect, as they claim that they are the people of intellect, their argument for mercy from reality would be more eloquent than their argument for will from reality. Is it clear? But the flaw and trial they have brought: they said that mercy means softness and tenderness, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is exalted above that?

Our answer to this comes from three aspects. The first aspect: we say that this implication applies only to the mercy of the created being, and the mercy of the Creator is not the mercy of the created being; we do not liken them. This is the first.

Second thing: we say that whoever claims gentleness and tenderness are negated from God is merely (...), and gentleness toward others in order to deliver kindness to them is not a attribute of deficiency.

The third aspect: we say that mercy is not the same as gentleness and tenderness. It may be that this king shows mercy, for example, to one of his subjects and is compassionate toward him, while he remains in his might and sovereignty, and does not feel within himself that in this state he has fallen from the rank of strength and resolve. Isn't that so? Say: no, or yes?!

* The students: Yes.

* The Shaykh: For example, this powerful king in his authority shows mercy to a poor person among the members of his nation, while he feels that he remains in his might and nothing has harmed it in that. Then we say, by reason...

(Ma) is a negating particle and not a Hijazi one here, because the negation was nullified by (illa). And Ibn Malik says:
Acting like laysa was given to ma, provided it is not followed by in, with the negation still remaining...
And here the negation has not remained.

And His saying: ﴿And what is this worldly life﴾ [al-'Ankabut 64]. The demonstrative here is for belittling and for the lowness of its rank. Using a demonstrative to belittle is found in the Arabic language, as in His saying about the disbelievers: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ [al-Anbiya' 36]; meaning: what is this contemptible, humiliated one who reviles the gods, when they are great and exalted, and the like.

And His saying: ﴿the worldly life﴾ is the abode in which we are, and it was described as "worldly" for two reasons: because it is near in time, and because it is near in rank.

And His saying ﴿the life﴾ came here to contrast it with the second life.

And His saying: ﴿except amusement and play﴾. This restriction is real: the world, which is the world, is confined to these two matters: amusement and play. As for the difference between them, it has been said: play is with the limbs, and amusement is with the tongue, based on the Most High's saying: ﴿And among the people is one who purchases idle talk to mislead from the way of Allah﴾ [Luqman 6]. And the Most High said: ﴿Those who are in vain discourse, playing﴾ [at-Tur 12].

It has also been said: amusement is in the heart, which is its heedlessness and its indulgence in diversions and in what distracts it from obedience to Allah, while play is in the limbs, of the tongue and other than the tongue. And this is closer to the truth: that amusement is in the hearts and play is in the limbs. This is the closer view.

Accordingly, the outcome of the world is that it is amusement with which a person diverts himself: heedlessness and wandering right and left. Likewise it is play, even the serious matters of the world are play, because they pass away and do not remain, or their owner departs from them. So it is like the play of children, who entertain themselves with it while they are children, then abandon it when they grow up, become wise, and recognize what they are upon.

The author said: (As for acts of devotion, they belong to the matters of the Hereafter, because their fruit appears there).

His saying: (As for acts of devotion) is an answer to an implied question, as if someone said: how can the world be amusement and play, when a person does righteous deeds in it: he prays, pays zakat, fasts, performs Hajj, honors his parents, maintains his kinship ties, and the like? Is this play?

* A student: No.

* The Shaykh: The author says: it is not play. Is this not in the world? He says: Yes, it is in the world, but its fruit appears in the Hereafter; therefore he said: (As for acts of devotion) -and they are from the world- (they belong to the matters of the Hereafter because their fruit appears there). The author spoke truly, for righteous deeds are not from the deeds of the world; therefore, if a person intends by them the world, they become void and he has no reward for them.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: whoever performs Hajj in order to take (worldly gain), then he has no share (khalaq) in the Hereafter; meaning, no portion. What the Shaykh said is confirmed by the Most High's saying: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein will be voided, and what they used to do is worthless﴾ [Hud 15-16].

It is also supported by his ﷺ saying: «Ruined is the servant of the dinar, ruined is the servant of the dirham» [Reported by al-Bukhari (2886) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah], and so on. The conclusion is that the deeds of the Hereafter are not from the deeds of the world; rather, if the deeds of the world are intended by them, they become void.

He said: ﴿And indeed the Hereafter abode, that is the true life﴾. This sentence is emphasized with three emphases. I say: explain to us the emphases in this.

* A student: The waw.

* The Shaykh: The waw is not for emphasis; the waw is not one of the emphasis particles.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: ﴿And indeed the Hereafter abode, that is the true life﴾.

* A student: (inna), and the lam, and the pronoun.

* The Shaykh: And the separating pronoun: ﴿that is the true life﴾. Note that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, emphasized that al-hayawan, meaning life, but it came in this pattern for intensification: (hayawan) is fa'alan for intensification; otherwise al-hayawan means life, and the pattern of (hayawan) is fa'alan, so the alif and nun were added for intensification.

His saying: ﴿And indeed the Hereafter abode﴾: it is what will be on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿that is the true life﴾: he said (meaning life), but the alif and nun were added to it for intensification; meaning it is the real life. Therefore the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection says: ﴿Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life﴾ [al-Fajr 24]. His life in the world, he sends forth for it; indeed it is his garden. But the real life is the life of the Hereafter, because the life of this world is in reality not life. First: because it is troubled, every purity in it has a turbidity. Second: because it does not remain, is it not so?
